modules.name: core
modules.about: The core library: what every module has without an import.

items.name: AbortController
items.doc: Cancels operations that take an AbortSignal (fetch(url, { signal }), streams): pass its signal along, call abort() to cancel them.

members.name: signal
members.doc: The signal to hand to the operations this controller cancels.

members.name: constructor
members.doc: A controller whose signal isn't aborted yet.

examples.code:
const c = new AbortController()
println(c.signal.aborted)   // false

members.name: abort
members.doc: Aborts the signal (once; later calls do nothing).

examples.code:
const c = new AbortController()
c.abort(new Error("no longer needed"))
println(c.signal.aborted)                    // true
println(c.signal.reason!.cause!.message)     // no longer needed

items.name: AbortError
items.doc: What an aborted operation throws.

members.name: constructor
members.doc: An AbortError with message (and no cause).

examples.code:
const e = new AbortError("download cancelled")
println(e.message)   // download cancelled

members.name: constructor
members.doc: An AbortError with message; cause is the reason given to abort, if any.

examples.code:
const e = new AbortError("download cancelled", new Error("user pressed stop"))
println(e.cause!.message)   // user pressed stop

items.name: AbortSignal
items.doc: Tells operations that they should stop (AbortController.signal).

examples.code:
const c = new AbortController()
const s = c.signal
s.onabort = () => println("stopping")
println(s.aborted)   // false
c.abort()            // stopping
println(s.aborted)   // true

members.name: aborted
members.doc: Whether it has been aborted.

members.name: reason
members.doc: Why it was aborted: an AbortError (with the reason as its cause).

members.name: onabort
members.doc: Called once when it's aborted (addEventListener("abort", …) adds more).

members.name: constructor
members.doc: A signal that isn't aborted (AbortController makes one; AbortSignal.abort and AbortSignal.timeout make others).

examples.code:
const s = new AbortSignal()
println(s.aborted)   // false

members.name: addEventListener
members.signature: public addEventListener(type: string, f: () => void): void
members.doc: Calls f when the signal is aborted (type must be "abort"); right away (as a microtask) if it already is.

members.name: throwIfAborted
members.doc: Throws the AbortError if it has been aborted.

members.name: abort
members.signature: public static abort(reason: Error? = null): AbortSignal
members.doc: A signal that is already aborted.

members.name: timeout
members.doc: A signal that aborts after ms milliseconds.

examples.code:
import { delay } from "std/timers"

const s = AbortSignal.timeout(10)
s.addEventListener("abort", () => println("timed out"))
await delay(50)               // timed out
println(s.reason!.cause!.message)   // The operation timed out

items.name: Addr
items.doc: An IP address and a port.

examples.code:
import { listen } from "std/net"

const listener = await listen(0, "127.0.0.1")
const addr: Addr = listener.addr
println(addr.hostname)   // 127.0.0.1
println(addr.port > 0)   // true (a free port the system picked)
listener.close()

members.name: hostname
members.doc: The IP address ("127.0.0.1", "::1", without brackets), or a Unix-domain socket's path.

members.name: port
members.doc: The port number; -1 for a Unix-domain socket.

items.name: Algorithm
items.doc: Web Crypto algorithm parameters, one struct for all of them (fields as the spec names them): { name: "AES-GCM", iv }, { name: "HMAC", hash: "SHA-256" }, { name: "ECDSA", hash: "SHA-256" }, { name: "ECDSA", namedCurve: "P-256" }, { name: "ECDH", public: key }, { name: "HKDF", hash, salt, info }, { name: "PBKDF2", hash, salt, iterations }, { name: "AES-GCM", length: 256 }.

members.name: name
members.doc: The algorithm's name ("AES-GCM", "HMAC", "ECDSA", "ECDH", "HKDF", "PBKDF2"; any case), or, for digest, the hash's.

members.name: hash
members.doc: The hash ("SHA-256", …) for HMAC, ECDSA, HKDF and PBKDF2. HMAC falls back on the key's.

members.name: namedCurve
members.doc: The curve for generateKey and importKey of ECDSA ("P-256", "P-384") and ECDH keys (also "X25519").

members.name: length
members.doc: The key length in bits for generateKey (AES-GCM: 128, 192 or 256; HMAC: 256 unless given).

members.name: iv
members.doc: AES-GCM's nonce (required; 12 bytes is usual), or AES-CBC's initialization vector (16 bytes).

members.name: counter
members.doc: AES-CTR's initial counter block (16 bytes); length is then how many of its rightmost bits count up (#69).

members.name: additionalData
members.doc: AES-GCM's authenticated, unencrypted data (none unless given).

members.name: tagLength
members.doc: AES-GCM's tag length in bits: only 128 (the default) is supported.

members.name: public
members.doc: ECDH's peer public key, for deriveBits.

members.name: salt
members.doc: The HKDF or PBKDF2 salt (empty unless given).

members.name: info
members.doc: HKDF's context info (empty unless given).

members.name: iterations
members.doc: PBKDF2's iteration count.

items.name: Arena
items.doc: Explicitly managed memory for unsafe code (spec §9.4): alloc hands out zeroed storage for plain data (no references), which the collector doesn't trace and which stays valid until free(). Pointers into it dangle afterwards (undefined behavior). The scoped arena { … } block needs none of this.

members.name: constructor
members.doc: An arena that reserves memory in chunks of capacity bytes (4096 if it isn't positive; a bigger allocation gets a chunk of its own).

members.name: alloc
members.doc: Room for count zeroed Ts (plain data: no references), as a pointer to the first.

members.name: free
members.doc: Frees everything allocated from this arena.

items.name: ArrayBuffer
items.doc: Raw bytes, off the GC heap.

members.name: byteLength
members.doc: Its size in bytes (0 once detached).

members.name: constructor
members.doc: byteLength zeroed bytes (a negative length gives an empty buffer).

members.name: constructor
members.doc: Takes over memory the runtime allocated (std/fs reads).

members.name: detached
members.doc: Whether it was transferred away (its length is then 0).

examples.code:
import { self } from "std/worker"

// In a worker module: hand the bytes to the parent instead of copying them.
const buf = new ArrayBuffer(8)
println(buf.detached)   // false
self.postMessage(buf, { transfer: [buf] })
println(buf.detached)     // true
println(buf.byteLength)   // 0

members.name: slice
members.signature: public slice(begin: int = 0, end: int? = null): ArrayBuffer
members.doc: A copy of bytes begin..end (negative counts from the end; end defaults to the end).

examples.code:
const buf = Uint8Array.from([10, 20, 30, 40]).buffer
const part = buf.slice(1, 3)
println(part.byteLength)   // 2
println(new Uint8Array(part, 0)[0])   // 20
println(buf.slice(-1).byteLength)     // 1

items.name: AsyncDisposable
items.doc: Released by await using (spec §11.5) at the end of its scope.

members.name: disposeAsync
members.doc: Releases the resource; await using waits for the promise.

items.name: AsyncIterator
items.signature: class AsyncIterator<T, E extends Error = never>
items.doc: An async iterator (spec §5.7): next() promises the next value, or null once done (so, like Iterator, a T that is itself nullable can't be told apart from the end). async function* g(): AsyncIterator<T> throws E makes one: its step function yields suspensions, both for await and, after storing the value, for yield v.

members.name: constructor
members.doc: An iterator with no steps (an async function* makes the ones that produce values).

members.name: next
members.doc: Promises the next value, or null once done. The promise rejects with what the generator throws (and later calls give null). Calls made before earlier ones are fulfilled queue up, in order.

members.name: asyncIterator
members.doc: for await uses the iterator itself.

items.name: Base64
items.doc: Base64 (RFC 4648 §4, or §5's URL-safe alphabet with url).

members.name: constructor
members.doc: A base64 codec (std/encoding exports one as base64).

examples.code:
const b64 = new Base64()
println(b64.encode(Uint8Array.from([1, 2, 3])))   // AQID

members.name: encode
members.signature: public encode(data: Uint8Array, url: bool = false): string
members.doc: data as base64; url uses - and _ and leaves out the = padding.

members.name: decode
members.signature: public decode(text: string): Uint8Array throws TypeError
members.doc: The bytes of base64 text (either alphabet, padding optional; whitespace is skipped). Other characters, or a length no encoding has, throw a TypeError.

items.name: BindOptions
items.doc: Options of bind (#214).

members.name: reuseAddress
members.doc: Lets other sockets bind the same address and port (SO_REUSEADDR, and SO_REUSEPORT where there is one), so several programs can receive one multicast group's datagrams.

items.name: BodyInit
items.signature: type BodyInit = string | Uint8Array | ReadableStream<Uint8Array> | URLSearchParams
items.doc: What a request or response body can be made from.

items.name: BuildInfo
items.doc: How the program is being built (spec §11.1).

members.name: mode
members.doc: "debug" or "release".

members.name: flags
members.doc: Flags given to the build (none yet).

items.name: CloseEvent
items.doc: How a connection ended: code (1000 normal, 1005 none given, 1006 lost), reason, and whether the closing handshake completed (wasClean).

examples.code:
const e = new CloseEvent(1000, "done", true)
println(`${e.type} ${e.code} ${e.reason} ${e.wasClean}`)   // close 1000 done true

members.name: type
members.doc: Always "close".

members.name: code
members.doc: The close code: the peer's, 1005 when its close frame had none, 1006 when the connection was lost or failed.

members.name: reason
members.doc: The peer's close reason ("" for none).

members.name: wasClean
members.doc: Whether the closing handshake completed.

members.name: constructor
members.signature: constructor(code: int, reason: string, wasClean: bool)
members.doc: A close event with code, reason and wasClean.

items.name: ComputedOptions
items.doc: What computed({ get, set }) takes: a getter and a setter (spec §16.3).

examples.code:
reactive celsius = 20.0
const fahrenheit = computed(ComputedOptions<f64> {
  get: () => celsius * 9.0 / 5.0 + 32.0,
  set: (f: f64) => { celsius = (f - 32.0) * 5.0 / 9.0 },
})
fahrenheit = 212.0
println(celsius)   // 100

members.name: get
members.doc: Computes the value from reactive state.

members.name: set
members.doc: Writing the computed value calls it.

items.name: Conn
items.doc: A TCP connection: chunks of bytes with read or for await, the rest as text with text(), writes (in the order they're made) with write/writeText. One read at a time.

members.name: localAddr
members.doc: This side's address.

members.name: remoteAddr
members.doc: The other side's address.

members.name: constructor
members.signature: constructor(fd: int, localAddr: Addr, remoteAddr: Addr)
members.doc: A connection on descriptor fd; made by connect and accept, not by programs.

members.name: readable
members.doc: The connection's incoming bytes as a stream (reading it and read() don't mix).

members.name: writable
members.doc: The connection's outgoing bytes as a stream: closing it finishes writing (closeWrite()), aborting it closes the connection.

members.name: read
members.doc: Up to n bytes (as soon as some arrive), or null once the other side has finished writing (or this side is closed).

members.name: next
members.doc: for await reads chunks until the end.

members.name: asyncIterator
members.doc: The connection itself (for await (const chunk of conn)).

members.name: text
members.doc: Everything until the other side finishes writing, as text (UTF-8; anything else rejects with kind "InvalidData").

members.name: write
members.doc: Writes all of data; the count written.

members.name: writeText
members.doc: Writes text as UTF-8; the count of bytes written.

members.name: setNoDelay
members.signature: public setNoDelay(noDelay: bool = true): void throws NetError
members.doc: Turns Nagle's algorithm off (noDelay, the default) or on: small writes go out at once instead of waiting to be coalesced (TCP_NODELAY, #65). Throws a NetError where the system can't (WASI).

members.name: setKeepAlive
members.signature: public setKeepAlive(enable: bool = false, initialDelay: int = 0): void throws NetError
members.doc: Turns TCP keep-alive probes on (enable) or off (#65); initialDelay is how long the connection idles before the first probe, in milliseconds (0: the system's default; rounded up to seconds). Throws a NetError where the system can't (WASI).

members.name: closeWrite
members.doc: Finishes writing once earlier writes are done (the other side reads the end); reading goes on.

members.name: close
members.doc: Closes the connection once earlier writes are done: a waiting read ends with null. Twice is fine.

items.name: Crypto
items.doc: The crypto global (Web Crypto): random values, UUIDs and subtle. A struct, so it costs programs that don't use it nothing.

members.name: subtle
members.doc: Web Crypto's asynchronous operations (keys, signatures, encryption, derivation).

members.name: getRandomValues
members.doc: Fills array with random bytes from the system and returns it (at most 65536 bytes, as on the Web).

examples.code:
const nonce = crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(12))
println(nonce.length)   // 12 (random bytes, different each run)

members.name: randomUUID
members.doc: A random version-4 UUID ("1b9d6bcd-bbfd-4b2d-9b5d-ab8dfbbd4bed").

items.name: CryptoError
items.doc: A failed cryptographic operation: a bad key or argument, or data that doesn't authenticate. kind is "InvalidArgument", "InvalidAccess" (a key used for something its usages don't allow), "AuthenticationFailed" or "Internal".

members.name: kind
members.doc: "InvalidArgument", "InvalidAccess", "AuthenticationFailed" or "Internal".

members.name: constructor
members.doc: An error of kind with message.

items.name: CryptoKey
items.doc: A key for crypto.subtle (Web Crypto): its algorithm, usages and bytes (raw secret bytes, a private scalar, or an uncompressed public point).

members.name: type
members.doc: "secret", "private" or "public".

members.name: extractable
members.doc: Whether exportKey may export a non-public key's bytes.

members.name: algorithm
members.doc: The algorithm the key is for, with its hash, curve or length.

members.name: usages
members.doc: What the key may be used for ("sign", "verify", "encrypt", "decrypt", "deriveBits"): another use rejects with an "InvalidAccess" CryptoError.

members.name: constructor
members.signature: constructor(type: string, extractable: bool, algorithm: KeyAlgorithm, usages: string[], bytes: Uint8Array)
members.doc: A key from its parts; crypto.subtle's generateKey and importKey make them.

items.name: CryptoKeyPair
items.doc: generateKey's result for key-pair algorithms.

members.name: publicKey
members.doc: The public key (always extractable).

members.name: privateKey
members.doc: The private key (extractable as generateKey was told).

items.name: DataView
items.doc: Reads and writes numbers of any size at any byte offset of a buffer, in either byte order: big-endian unless littleEndian is given, as on the Web. Offsets outside the view panic (the Web throws a RangeError). 64-bit integers are i64/u64 (getBigInt64, getBigUint64: the Web's names, without its BigInt). Pico also takes a Uint8Array: the view's bytes.

examples.code:
const view = new DataView(new ArrayBuffer(6))
view.setUint16(0, 0xCAFE)
view.setUint32(2, 1, true)
println(view.getUint8(0))          // 202
println(view.getUint16(0, true))   // 65226
println(view.getUint32(2, true))   // 1

members.name: buffer
members.doc: The ArrayBuffer whose bytes the view reads and writes.

members.name: byteOffset
members.doc: Where the view starts in buffer, in bytes.

members.name: constructor
members.signature: constructor(buffer: ArrayBuffer, byteOffset: int = 0, byteLength: int? = null)
members.doc: A view of buffer from byteOffset, byteLength bytes long (default: to its end). Panics if that isn't inside the buffer.

members.name: constructor
members.doc: A view of the same bytes as view.

members.name: byteLength
members.doc: The view's size in bytes (0 once the buffer is detached).

examples.code:
const view = new DataView(new ArrayBuffer(12), 4)
println(view.byteLength)   // 8

members.name: getUint16
members.signature: public getUint16(at: int, littleEndian: bool = false): int

examples.code:
const view = new DataView(new ArrayBuffer(2))
view.setUint16(0, 513)
println(view.getUint16(0))         // 513
println(view.getUint16(0, true))   // 258 (the bytes read little-endian)

members.name: getInt16
members.signature: public getInt16(at: int, littleEndian: bool = false): int

examples.code:
const view = new DataView(new ArrayBuffer(2))
view.setInt16(0, -2)
println(view.getInt16(0))         // -2
println(view.getInt16(0, true))   // -257 (the bytes read little-endian)

members.name: getUint32
members.signature: public getUint32(at: int, littleEndian: bool = false): int

examples.code:
const view = new DataView(new ArrayBuffer(4))
view.setUint32(0, 3000000000)
println(view.getUint32(0))         // 3000000000
println(view.getUint32(0, true))   // 6213810 (the bytes read little-endian)

members.name: getInt32
members.signature: public getInt32(at: int, littleEndian: bool = false): int

examples.code:
const view = new DataView(new ArrayBuffer(4))
view.setInt32(0, -100000)
println(view.getInt32(0))         // -100000
println(view.getInt32(0, true))   // 1618607871 (the bytes read little-endian)

members.name: getBigInt64
members.signature: public getBigInt64(at: int, littleEndian: bool = false): i64

members.name: getBigUint64
members.signature: public getBigUint64(at: int, littleEndian: bool = false): u64

members.name: getFloat16
members.signature: public getFloat16(at: int, littleEndian: bool = false): f64
members.doc: An IEEE 754 half-precision number (ES2025's getFloat16).

examples.code:
const view = new DataView(Uint8Array.from([0x3C, 0x00]))
println(view.getFloat16(0))   // 1

members.name: getFloat32
members.signature: public getFloat32(at: int, littleEndian: bool = false): f32

members.name: getFloat64
members.signature: public getFloat64(at: int, littleEndian: bool = false): f64

members.name: setUint8
members.signature: public setUint8(at: int, value: int): void
members.doc: Stores value's low 8 bits (as do all the integer setters: their low 16, 32, 64 bits).

examples.code:
const view = new DataView(new ArrayBuffer(2))
view.setUint8(0, 200)
println(view.getUint8(0))   // 200
println(view.getUint8(0))    // 200

members.name: setInt8
members.signature: public setInt8(at: int, value: int): void

examples.code:
const view = new DataView(new ArrayBuffer(2))
view.setInt8(0, -3)
println(view.getInt8(0))   // -3
println(view.getUint8(0))    // 253

members.name: setUint16
members.signature: public setUint16(at: int, value: int, littleEndian: bool = false): void

examples.code:
const view = new DataView(new ArrayBuffer(2))
view.setUint16(0, 513, true)     // little-endian
println(view.getUint16(0, true))   // 513
println(view.getUint8(0))          // 1

members.name: setInt16
members.signature: public setInt16(at: int, value: int, littleEndian: bool = false): void

examples.code:
const view = new DataView(new ArrayBuffer(2))
view.setInt16(0, -2, true)     // little-endian
println(view.getInt16(0, true))   // -2
println(view.getUint8(0))          // 254

members.name: setUint32
members.signature: public setUint32(at: int, value: int, littleEndian: bool = false): void

examples.code:
const view = new DataView(new ArrayBuffer(4))
view.setUint32(0, 3000000000, true)     // little-endian
println(view.getUint32(0, true))   // 3000000000
println(view.getUint8(0))          // 0

members.name: setInt32
members.signature: public setInt32(at: int, value: int, littleEndian: bool = false): void

examples.code:
const view = new DataView(new ArrayBuffer(4))
view.setInt32(0, -100000, true)     // little-endian
println(view.getInt32(0, true))   // -100000
println(view.getUint8(0))          // 96

members.name: setBigInt64
members.signature: public setBigInt64(at: int, value: i64, littleEndian: bool = false): void

members.name: setBigUint64
members.signature: public setBigUint64(at: int, value: u64, littleEndian: bool = false): void

examples.code:
const big: u64 = 18446744073709551615
const view = new DataView(new ArrayBuffer(8))
view.setBigUint64(0, big)
println(view.getBigUint64(0))   // 18446744073709551615
println(view.getInt8(0))        // -1

members.name: setFloat16
members.signature: public setFloat16(at: int, value: f64, littleEndian: bool = false): void
members.doc: value rounded to the nearest half-precision number (ties to even; too large: infinity).

members.name: setFloat32
members.signature: public setFloat32(at: int, value: f32, littleEndian: bool = false): void

examples.code:
const view = new DataView(new ArrayBuffer(4))
view.setFloat32(0, 1.5, true)
println(view.getUint8(3))           // 63
println(view.getFloat32(0, true))   // 1.5

items.name: Datagram
items.doc: A received datagram and where it came from.

members.name: data
members.doc: The datagram's bytes (cut to the size receive asked for).

members.name: addr

items.name: Date
items.doc: JavaScript's Date: a time value in milliseconds since 1970 (NaN when invalid), seen in local time or UTC. Kept so ported code works; new code should use std/time.

members.name: constructor
members.signature: constructor(value: number | string | Date | null = null, month: number? = null, day: number = 1, hours: number = 0, minutes: number = 0, seconds: number = 0, ms: number = 0)
members.doc: new Date() is now; new Date(ms) a time value; new Date("…") parses (as Date.parse); new Date(y, m, …) is a local date with a 0-based month.

members.name: now
members.doc: Milliseconds since 1970 now.

members.name: UTC
members.signature: public static UTC(year: number, month: number = 0, day: number = 1, hours: number = 0, minutes: number = 0, seconds: number = 0, ms: number = 0): number
members.doc: The time value of a UTC date (0-based month), like the constructor's local form.

examples.code:
const t = Date.UTC(2024, 2, 10, 12, 30)
println(t)                            // 1710073800000
println(new Date(t).toISOString())    // 2024-03-10T12:30:00.000Z
println(Date.UTC(2024))               // 1704067200000

members.name: parse
members.doc: Parses ISO 8601 (2024-03-10, 2024-03-10T12:30:00.5Z, …+01:00; date-only forms are UTC, date-times without an offset local) and toString/toUTCString output. NaN when it can't.

members.name: getTime
members.doc: The time value: milliseconds since 1970 (UTC), or NaN for an invalid date.

members.name: valueOf
members.doc: The time value, as getTime().

members.name: getFullYear
members.doc: The full year (2024; not 2-digit), in local time; NaN for an invalid date.

examples.code:
const d = new Date(2024, 4, 15)
println(d.getFullYear())   // 2024

members.name: getMonth
members.doc: The month, 0–11 (January is 0), in local time; NaN for an invalid date.

examples.code:
const d = new Date(2024, 4, 15)
println(d.getMonth())   // 4 (May: months are 0-based)

members.name: getDate
members.doc: The day of the month, 1–31, in local time; NaN for an invalid date.

examples.code:
const d = new Date(2024, 4, 15)
println(d.getDate())   // 15

members.name: getDay
members.doc: The day of the week, 0–6 (Sunday is 0), in local time; NaN for an invalid date.

examples.code:
const d = new Date(2024, 4, 15)
println(d.getDay())   // 3 (Wednesday; Sunday is 0)

members.name: getHours
members.doc: The hour, 0–23, in local time; NaN for an invalid date.

examples.code:
const d = new Date(2024, 4, 15, 9, 45, 30)
println(d.getHours())   // 9

members.name: getMinutes
members.doc: The minutes, 0–59, in local time; NaN for an invalid date.

examples.code:
const d = new Date(2024, 4, 15, 9, 45, 30)
println(d.getMinutes())   // 45

members.name: getSeconds
members.doc: The seconds, 0–59, in local time; NaN for an invalid date.

examples.code:
const d = new Date(2024, 4, 15, 9, 45, 30)
println(d.getSeconds())   // 30

members.name: getMilliseconds
members.doc: The milliseconds, 0–999, in local time; NaN for an invalid date.

examples.code:
const d = new Date(2024, 4, 15, 9, 45, 30, 125)
println(d.getMilliseconds())   // 125

members.name: getUTCFullYear
members.doc: The full year (2024; not 2-digit), in UTC; NaN for an invalid date.

examples.code:
const d = new Date("2024-12-31T23:30:00Z")
println(d.getUTCFullYear())   // 2024

members.name: getUTCMonth
members.doc: The month, 0–11 (January is 0), in UTC; NaN for an invalid date.

examples.code:
const d = new Date("2024-03-10T12:30:00Z")
println(d.getUTCMonth())   // 2 (March: months are 0-based)

members.name: getUTCDate
members.doc: The day of the month, 1–31, in UTC; NaN for an invalid date.

examples.code:
const d = new Date("2024-03-10T12:30:00Z")

members.name: getUTCDay

items.name: Performance
items.doc: performance (High Resolution Time): now() is milliseconds since the program started. (A struct, so the global costs programs that don't use it nothing.)

examples.code:
const start = performance.now()
let sum = 0
for (let i = 0; i < 1000; i++) sum += i
const elapsed = performance.now() - start
println(sum)              // 499500
println(elapsed >= 0.0)   // true

members.doc: Milliseconds (with a fraction) since the program started.

members.doc: When the program started, in milliseconds since 1970.

items.name: Promise
items.signature: class Promise<T, E extends Error = never>
items.doc: A value that arrives later (spec §10.1): settles once, with a T or an error. E is what awaiting it can throw (an async function's throws). await p waits for it inside an async function (or at the top level); reactions run as microtasks, so the ordering is JavaScript's. An async function f(): Promise<T> throws E returns a Promise<T, E>.

members.name: constructor
members.doc: A pending promise (what an async function settles).

examples.code:
const p = new Promise<int>()
println(p.settled)   // false

members.name: constructor
members.signature: constructor(executor: (resolve: (value: T) => void, reject: (error: Error) => void) => void)
members.doc: new Promise((resolve, reject) => …): executor runs right away and settles it.

members.name: settled
members.doc: Whether it has settled (fulfilled or rejected).

members.name: then
members.signature: public then<U>(f: (value: T) => U): Promise<U, E>
members.doc: A promise of f(value), settled after this one (rejected with its error).

examples.code:
const doubled = Promise.resolve(21).then((n) => n * 2)
println(await doubled)   // 42

members.name: catch
members.doc: A promise of this one's value, or of f(error) when it rejects (so it doesn't reject): load().catch((e) => fallback) (#52).

members.name: finally
members.doc: A promise that settles like this one, after f ran (once it settled either way) (#52).

examples.code:
const p = Promise.resolve("done").finally(() => println("cleaning up"))
println(await p)   // cleaning up, then: done

members.name: resolve
members.doc: A promise already fulfilled with value.

examples.code:
const p = Promise.resolve("cached")
println(await p)   // cached

members.name: reject
members.signature: public static reject<U>(error: Error): Promise<U, Error>
members.doc: A promise already rejected with error.

members.name: all
members.signature: public static all<U, F extends Error>(ps: Promise<U, F>[]): Promise<U[], F>
members.doc: All the values, in order; rejected with the first error.

members.name: race
members.signature: public static race<U, F extends Error>(ps: Promise<U, F>[]): Promise<U, F>
members.doc: Settles like the first of ps to settle.

members.name: withResolvers
members.signature: public static withResolvers<U, F extends Error>(): PromiseWithResolvers<U, F>
members.doc: A pending promise and the functions that settle it (ES2024), for code that settles it from outside an executor: const r = Promise.withResolvers<int, Error>(), then r.resolve(1).

members.name: allSettled
members.signature: public static allSettled<U, F extends Error>(ps: Promise<U, F>[]): Promise<Settled<U>[]>
members.doc: Waits for all of ps, never rejecting: how each one ended.

items.name: PromiseWithResolvers
items.doc: What Promise.withResolvers() gives: the promise and the functions that settle it (the first call of either wins).

members.name: promise
members.doc: The pending promise.

members.name: resolve
members.doc: Fulfills the promise with value.

examples.code:
const r = Promise.withResolvers<int, Error>()
r.resolve(1)
r.resolve(2)               // ignored: the first call wins
println(await r.promise)   // 1

members.name: reject
members.doc: Rejects the promise with error.

items.name: QueuingStrategy
items.doc: How many chunks a stream queues before it asks its source to wait (highWaterMark).

members.name: highWaterMark
members.doc: The number of chunks (default 1; a TransformStream's readable side defaults to 0).

items.name: RangeError
items.doc: A value outside the allowed range, as JavaScript's.

members.name: constructor
members.doc: A RangeError with message.

examples.code:
const e = new RangeError("index 7 out of range")
println(e.message)   // index 7 out of range

items.name: Reactive
items.doc: A reactive cell (spec §16.1): what a reactive declaration holds and computed returns. Reads and writes of a reactive binding go through __get and __set.

examples.code:
// Cells come from `reactive` declarations and `computed`, not from this constructor.
reactive score = 10
const cell: Reactive<int> = score
cell = 20
println(score)   // 20

items.name: ReadResult
items.doc: What a reader's read() gives: a chunk, or done at the end.

members.name: done
members.doc: Whether the stream has ended (then there's no value).

members.name: value
members.doc: The chunk, or null at the end.

items.name: ReadableStream
items.doc: A stream of chunks to read: with a reader (getReader()), for await, or piped into a WritableStream.

members.name: constructor
members.doc: A stream fed by source (its start runs right away), queuing up to strategy.highWaterMark chunks (default 1).

members.name: from
members.doc: A stream of items, in order.

members.name: from
members.doc: A stream of what iterator items (a generator's, say) yields, read as it's pulled (#63).

members.name: from
members.signature: public static from<U, F extends Error>(items: AsyncIterator<U, F>): ReadableStream<U>
members.doc: A stream of what async iterator items (an async generator's, say) yields, awaited as it's pulled (#63); its error errors the stream.

members.name: tee
members.doc: Two streams that each get every chunk of this one, which is locked from then on (#63). A chunk is read when either branch wants one, and waits in the other branch's queue until that one reads it. An error fails both; cancelling both cancels this stream.

members.name: locked
members.doc: Whether a reader (or a pipe) holds the stream.

members.name: getReader
members.doc: A reader for the stream (only one at a time).

members.name: next
members.doc: for await reads the chunks (while no reader holds the stream).

examples.code:
const s = ReadableStream.from([7, 8])
println(await s.next())   // 7
println(await s.next())   // 8
println(await s.next())   // null

members.name: asyncIterator
members.doc: for await uses the stream itself (see next).

members.name: cancel
members.signature: public cancel(reason: Error? = null): Promise<void, Error>
members.doc: Gives up on the stream: queued chunks are dropped, waiting reads get the end, and the source's cancel runs.

members.name: pipeTo
members.signature: public async pipeTo(dest: WritableStream<T>, options: StreamPipeOptions = {}): Promise<void> throws Error
members.doc: Writes every chunk to dest, then closes it (see StreamPipeOptions). Rejects with the error of either side.

examples.code:
const lines: string[] = []
const sink = new WritableStream<string>({
  write: (chunk, _c) => lines.push(chunk),
  close: () => println("closed"),
})
await ReadableStream.from(["a", "b", "c"]).pipeTo(sink)   // closed
println(lines.join(","))   // a,b,c

members.name: pipeThrough
members.signature: public pipeThrough<O>(t: TransformStream<T, O>, options: StreamPipeOptions = {}): ReadableStream<O>
members.doc: Pipes the stream into t's writable side; its readable side.

items.name: ReadableStreamDefaultController
items.doc: What a source uses to feed its stream.

members.name: constructor
members.doc: (Made by the stream, for its source.)

members.name: desiredSize
members.doc: How many more chunks fit before the high-water mark (0 or less: wait).

members.name: enqueue
members.doc: Adds chunk to the stream (straight to a waiting read, if any). Panics once the stream is closed, failed or closing.

members.name: close
members.doc: Ends the stream once the queued chunks are read.

members.name: error
members.doc: Fails the stream: queued chunks are dropped and reads reject with e.

items.name: ReadableStreamDefaultReader
items.doc: Reads a ReadableStream (which it locks until releaseLock()).

examples.code:
const reader: ReadableStreamDefaultReader<int> = ReadableStream.from([1, 2]).getReader()
println((await reader.read()).value)   // 1
println((await reader.read()).value)   // 2
println((await reader.read()).done)    // true

members.name: constructor
members.doc: A reader that locks stream; panics if the stream is already locked.

members.name: read
members.doc: The next chunk ({ done: false, value }), or { done: true } at the end.

members.name: cancel
members.signature: public cancel(reason: Error? = null): Promise<void, Error>
members.doc: Cancels the stream (see ReadableStream.cancel); the lock stays held. Panics after releaseLock().

members.name: closed
members.doc: Settles when the stream closes (rejects when it fails).

examples.code:
const reader = ReadableStream.from([1]).getReader()
println((await reader.read()).value)   // 1
await reader.closed
println("closed")                      // closed

members.name: releaseLock
members.doc: Unlocks the stream (another reader, or for await, can take it).

items.name: RegExp
items.doc: A regular expression: /pattern/flags or new RegExp(pattern, flags) (flags d, g, i, m, s, u, v, y).

members.name: source
members.doc: The pattern's text ("(?:)" for an empty pattern).

members.name: flags
members.doc: The flags, in canonical order ("dgimsuvy").

members.name: lastIndex
members.doc: Where the next exec or test starts with the g or y flag, in code points; other regexes ignore it.

members.name: constructor
members.signature: constructor(pattern: string, flags: string = "") throws SyntaxError
members.doc: Throws a SyntaxError for an invalid pattern or flags.

members.name: constructor
members.signature: constructor(other: RegExp, flags: string? = null) throws SyntaxError
members.doc: A copy of other: its pattern with its flags, or with flags instead (#62). Its lastIndex starts at 0.

examples.code:
const re = /a+/g
println(new RegExp(re))         // /a+/g
println(new RegExp(re, "i"))    // /a+/i

members.name: global
members.doc: Whether the g flag is set (find every match).

examples.code:
println(/o/g.global)   // true
println(/o/.global)    // false

members.name: ignoreCase
members.doc: Whether the i flag is set (case-insensitive).

examples.code:
const re = /hello/i
println(re.ignoreCase)      // true
println(re.test("HeLLo"))   // true

members.name: multiline
members.doc: Whether the m flag is set (^ and $ also match at line breaks).

examples.code:
const re = /^b/m
println(re.multiline)        // true
println(re.test("a\nb"))     // true

members.name: dotAll
members.doc: Whether the s flag is set (. also matches line breaks).

examples.code:
const re = /a.b/s
println(re.dotAll)          // true
println(re.test("a\nb"))    // true

members.name: unicode
members.doc: Whether the u flag is set.

examples.code:
println(/x/u.unicode)   // true
println(/x/.unicode)    // false

members.name: sticky
members.doc: Whether the y flag is set (a match only at lastIndex).

examples.code:
const re = /\d/y
println(re.sticky)      // true
println(re.test("a1"))  // false
re.lastIndex = 1
println(re.test("a1"))  // true

members.name: hasIndices
members.doc: Whether the d flag is set.

examples.code:
println(/x/d.hasIndices)   // true
println(/x/.hasIndices)    // false

members.name: exec
members.doc: The next match in s (from lastIndex with g or y, which it then moves past the match, or back to 0 when there's none).

members.name: test
members.doc: Whether s has a match (moving lastIndex as exec does).

examples.code:
const digits = /^\d+$/
println(digits.test("123"))   // true
println(digits.test("12a"))   // false

members.name: toString
members.doc: /source/flags.

examples.code:
const re = new RegExp("a/b", "gi")
println(re.toString())   // /a\/b/gi
println(re.source)       // a\/b
println(re.flags)        // gi

items.name: RegExpIndices
items.doc: Where a d-flag match and its groups are (RegExpMatch.indices, #62): [start, end] in code points per element (null for a group that didn't take part), and by group name.

members.name: groups

import { bind } from "std/net"

const xs = new Uint32Array(3)
xs.set(0, 4000000000)

bytes.set(0, 0xCA)

println(bytes[0])               // 202
println(bytes.includes(0xFE))   // true

members.name: BYTES_PER_ELEMENT
members.doc: The size of an element: 1 byte.

members.name: buffer
members.doc: The ArrayBuffer whose bytes the view reads and writes.

members.name: constructor

members.signature: constructor(buffer: ArrayBuffer, byteOffset: int, length: int)
members.doc: A view of length elements of buffer from byteOffset. Panics if byteOffset is negative, length is negative, or the view would end past the buffer.

members.name: length
members.doc: 0 once the buffer is detached (transferred).

const bytes = Uint8Array.from([1, 2, 3])
println(bytes.length)   // 3

members.doc: The view's size in bytes (length * 1; 0 once the buffer is detached).

examples.code:
const bytes = new Uint8Array(5)
println(bytes.byteLength)   // 5

members.name: get
members.doc: The byte at i (0 to 255); panics if i is out of bounds.

members.signature: public set(i: int, value: int): void
members.doc: Sets the byte at i to value's low 8 bits (value modulo 256); panics if i is out of bounds.

const bytes = new Uint8Array(2)
bytes.set(0, 65)
bytes.set(1, 257)       // stored as 1
println(bytes[0])       // 65

members.signature: public subarray(begin: int = 0, end: int? = null): Uint8Array
members.doc: A view of the same bytes from begin to end (negative counts from the end).

members.signature: public setAll(source: Uint8Array, offset: int = 0): void

const out = new Uint8Array(5)
out.setAll(Uint8Array.from([7, 8]), 2)

const bytes = Uint8Array.from([1, 2, 3, 4, 5])
bytes.copyWithin(0, 3)
println(bytes[0])   // 4

members.signature: public indexOf(value: int, fromIndex: int = 0): int
members.doc: The first position from fromIndex (negative counts from the end) whose byte is value, or -1, as on the Web.

const bytes = Uint8Array.from([10, 20, 30, 20])
println(bytes.indexOf(20))      // 1
println(bytes.indexOf(20, 2))   // 3
println(bytes.indexOf(99))      // -1

members.signature: public includes(value: int, fromIndex: int = 0): bool
members.doc: Whether a byte from fromIndex on is value.

members.signature: public fill(value: int, start: int = 0, end: int? = null): Uint8Array
members.doc: Sets the bytes from start to end (negative counts from the end) to value's low 8 bits, as on the Web. Returns this view.

examples.code:
const bytes = new Uint8Array(4).fill(255, 1, 3)
println(bytes[0])   // 0
println(bytes[1])   // 255
println(bytes[3])   // 0

members.name: equals
members.doc: Whether other has the same bytes (and length). Not on the Web, where it takes a loop.

members.name: from
members.doc: The bytes of values (each taken modulo 256).

items.name: UnderlyingSink
items.doc: The sink behind a WritableStream: start runs at once, write (or writeAsync) gets each chunk in turn, close (or closeAsync) runs after the last, abort when the writer gives up.

members.name: start
members.doc: Runs once, inside the constructor.

members.name: write
members.doc: Takes a chunk; the next one comes after it returns.

members.name: writeAsync
members.signature: writeAsync?: (chunk: T, c: WritableStreamDefaultController) => Promise<void, Error>
members.doc: Like write, but finishes when the promise settles; a rejection fails the stream. Used instead of write when both are given.

members.name: close
members.doc: Runs after the last queued chunk is written, when the stream is closed.

members.name: closeAsync
members.doc: Like close, but finishes when the promise settles; a rejection fails the stream. Used instead of close when both are given.

members.name: abort
members.doc: Called with the reason when the stream is aborted (before the queued writes reject).

items.name: UnderlyingSource
items.doc: The source behind a ReadableStream: start runs at once, pull (or pullAsync) when the stream wants more chunks, cancel when its reader gives up.

members.name: start
members.doc: Runs once, inside the constructor (it can already enqueue chunks).

members.name: pull
members.doc: Called when the stream wants more chunks (a waiting read, or room below the high-water mark); not again while it runs. The first call comes after start, as a microtask.

members.name: pullAsync
members.doc: Like pull, but finishes when the promise settles (not called again until then); a rejection fails the stream. Used instead of pull when both are given.

members.name: cancel
members.doc: Called with the reason when the stream is cancelled.

items.name: WatchHandle
items.doc: Stops an effect (spec §16.4).

examples.code:
reactive count = 0
const handle = watchEffect(() => println(`count is ${count}`))   // count is 0
count = 1          // count is 1
handle.dispose()
count = 2          // prints nothing

reactive n = 0
const handle: WatchHandle = watchEffect(() => println(n))   // 0
handle.dispose()

members.name: dispose
members.doc: Stops the effect; disposing it again does nothing.

examples.code:
reactive n = 0
const h = watchEffect(() => println(`n = ${n}`))   // n = 0
n = 1              // n = 1
h.dispose()
h.dispose()        // does nothing
n = 2              // prints nothing

items.name: WeakMap
items.doc: A map whose keys are held weakly: an entry goes away with its key. Values are held strongly, so a value that refers to its own key keeps the entry (no ephemerons yet).

members.name: constructor

members.name: has
members.doc: Whether the map has an entry for key.

members.name: get
members.doc: The value for key, or null if there's none.

members.name: set
members.signature: public set(key: K, value: V): WeakMap<K, V>
members.doc: Sets key's value; the map itself.

members.name: delete
members.doc: Removes key's entry; whether there was one.

items.name: WeakRef
items.doc: A reference that doesn't keep its target alive.

members.name: constructor
members.doc: A reference to target.

members.name: deref
members.doc: The target, or null once it has been collected.

items.name: WeakSet
items.doc: A set whose members are held weakly.

members.name: constructor
members.doc: An empty set.

members.name: has

members.name: add
