items.name: WebSocket
items.doc: A WebSocket connection. Assign onopen, onmessage, onclose and onerror right after creating it (they're called from the event loop); send text or bytes once it's open.

members.name: CONNECTING
members.doc: readyState 0: the handshake hasn't finished yet.

examples.code:
const ws = new WebSocket("ws://127.0.0.1:9/")
println(ws.readyState == WebSocket.CONNECTING)   // true (just created)
println(WebSocket.CONNECTING)                    // 0
ws.close()

members.name: OPEN
members.doc: readyState 1: messages can be sent and received.

members.name: CLOSING
members.doc: readyState 2: close() started the closing handshake.

members.name: CLOSED
members.doc: readyState 3: the connection is closed (or never opened).

members.name: url
members.doc: The URL connected to, normalized (as URL.href); "" for a server-side socket.

members.name: readyState
members.doc: The connection's state: CONNECTING, OPEN, CLOSING or CLOSED (0–3).

members.name: protocol
members.doc: The subprotocol the server chose ("" for none).

members.name: onopen
members.doc: Called once the connection is open (an "open" event).

members.name: onmessage
members.doc: Called for each message received while the socket is open (fragmented ones arrive whole).

members.name: onclose
members.doc: Called once when the connection ends, cleanly or not.

members.name: onerror
members.doc: Called when connecting fails (an "error" event), just before onclose with code 1006.

members.name: constructor
members.signature: constructor(url: string, protocols: string[] = [], options: WebSocketOptions = {}) throws TypeError
members.doc: Connects to url (ws:/wss:, or http:/https: as the same). An invalid URL or another scheme throws a TypeError. (pico) options.caCerts adds trusted certificates (PEM) for wss:.

members.name: send
members.doc: Sends a text or binary message. Panics before the socket is open.

members.name: close
members.signature: public close(code: int = 1000, reason: string = ""): void
members.doc: Starts the closing handshake (code 1000 or 3000–4999, reason at most 123 bytes).

items.name: WebSocketOptions
items.doc: new WebSocket(url, protocols, options) (a pico extension): extra trusted certificates (PEM) for wss:.

members.name: caCerts
members.doc: Extra trusted certificates (PEM) for wss:, besides the system's roots.

members.name: maxMessageBytes
members.doc: The largest message to receive, in bytes (its fragments together; #67): a bigger one closes the connection with code 1009 before it's read. No limit by default.

items.name: Worker
items.signature: class Worker<In extends Sendable, Out extends Sendable, E extends Error = never>
items.doc: A worker thread running a module: new Worker<In, Out>("./job") (the compiler turns the path into the module's id). It receives Ins and sends Outs. An inline worker, new Worker(f), runs a capture-free function: await w.call(x) is f(x), computed in the worker (throwing what f throws, E).

members.name: onmessage
members.doc: Called with each message the worker sends (inline workers' replies settle call's promises instead).

members.name: onerror
members.doc: Called when the worker ends by a panic or an uncaught error; without it, the error ends the program like an uncaught one.

members.name: constructor
members.doc: (new Worker("./job"): module is the module's id; kind is 0.)

members.name: constructor
members.doc: new Worker(f): an inline worker that serves calls with f, a capture-free function copied to the worker. While no call is pending it doesn't keep the program running.

examples.code:
const w = new Worker((s: string): int => s.length)
println(await w.call("hello"))   // 5

members.name: call
members.doc: An inline worker's f(input), computed in the worker.

members.name: postMessage
members.signature: public postMessage(message: In, options: TransferOptions? = null): void
members.doc: Sends a copy of message to the worker (options.transfer: buffers moved instead). Only for a worker module: an inline worker (new Worker(f)) takes calls, and this panics.

members.name: terminate
members.doc: Stops the worker (right away: at its next safepoint). Pending calls reject with a WorkerPanicked.

items.name: WorkerPanicked
items.doc: A worker ended by a panic or an uncaught error (Worker.onerror).

members.name: constructor
members.doc: A WorkerPanicked with the panic's or the uncaught error's message.

examples.code:
const e = new WorkerPanicked("the worker was terminated")
println(e.message)   // the worker was terminated

items.name: WritableStream
items.doc: A destination for chunks: through a writer (getWriter()), or as a pipe's end.

members.name: constructor
members.doc: A stream writing to sink (its start runs right away), with room for strategy.highWaterMark chunks (default 1) before writers see backpressure.

members.name: locked
members.doc: Whether a writer (or a pipe) holds the stream.

members.name: getWriter
members.doc: A writer for the stream (only one at a time).

members.name: close
members.doc: Closes the stream after the queued writes (when no writer holds it).

members.name: abort
members.signature: public abort(reason: Error? = null): Promise<void, Error>
members.doc: Fails the stream at once: queued writes reject, and the sink's abort runs.

items.name: WritableStreamDefaultController
items.doc: What a sink uses to fail its stream.

members.name: constructor
members.doc: (Made by the stream, for its sink.)

members.name: error
members.doc: Fails the stream: waiting and later writes reject with e.

items.name: WritableStreamDefaultWriter
items.doc: Writes to a WritableStream (which it locks until releaseLock()).

members.name: constructor
members.doc: A writer that locks stream; panics if the stream is already locked.

members.name: write
members.doc: Queues chunk; settles once the sink has taken it.

members.name: close
members.doc: Closes the stream after the queued writes.

members.name: abort
members.signature: public abort(reason: Error? = null): Promise<void, Error>
members.doc: Aborts the stream (see WritableStream.abort). Panics after releaseLock().

members.name: ready
members.doc: Settles when there's room for another chunk (backpressure).

members.name: desiredSize
members.doc: How many more chunks fit before the high-water mark.

members.name: closed
members.doc: Settles when the stream closes (rejects when it fails).

members.name: releaseLock
members.doc: Unlocks the stream (another writer can take it); using this writer afterwards panics.

items.name: assert
items.signature: function assert(cond: bool, message?: string): void
items.doc:
Panics when cond is false, with message (or assertion failed) and where the assertion is.

A panic means a bug: it can't be caught, runs finally blocks while unwinding, and on the main thread ends the process (exit code 101) with the message and a stack trace. For failures a caller should handle, throw an error instead.

examples.code:
const xs = [1, 2, 3]
assert(xs.length == 3, "three elements")
println("ok")   // ok

items.name: clearInterval
items.doc: Stops the setInterval calls whose id is id.

items.name: clearTimeout
items.doc: Cancels the setTimeout call whose id is id (nothing happens if it already ran or was cleared).

items.name: computed
items.doc: A value computed from reactive state (spec §16.3): getter runs when the value is read and something it read changed since; otherwise the cached value is returned. Read-only.

examples.code:
reactive first = "Ada"
reactive last = "Lovelace"
const full = computed(() => `${first} ${last}`)
println(full)   // Ada Lovelace
last = "Byron"
println(full)   // Ada Byron

items.name: computed
items.doc: A computed value that can be written: writing it calls options.set (spec §16.3).

items.name: derive
items.doc: equals, hashCode and compareTo for a class, field by field in declaration order (only the class's own fields). Structs, enums and tuples have them already.

items.name: effectScope
items.doc: Runs fn now; the effects, computeds and effect scopes it creates belong to the returned scope (spec §16.7).

items.name: eprint
items.doc: Writes text to stderr at once, after what print wrote (#157).

examples.code:
eprint("warning: ")
eprintln("disk almost full")   // stderr: warning: disk almost full

items.name: eprintln
items.doc: eprint with a line break.

examples.code: eprintln("something went wrong")   // written to stderr

items.name: fetch
items.signature: async function fetch(input: string | URL | Request, init: RequestInit = {}): Promise<Response> throws Error
items.doc: Fetches input over HTTP/1.1, following redirects (see RequestInit.redirect). Network failures and unsupported URLs reject with a TypeError (its cause is the NetError); HTTP error statuses don't (check ok).

items.name: navigator
items.doc: What the machine offers (navigator.hardwareConcurrency, as on the Web).

examples.code:
const n = navigator.hardwareConcurrency
println(`up to ${n} workers in parallel`)   // e.g. up to 8 workers in parallel

members.name: hardwareConcurrency
members.doc: The number of processors.

examples.code: println(navigator.hardwareConcurrency > 0)   // true

items.name: panic
items.doc:
Stops the current thread with message: a bug, not an error to handle.

A panic can't be caught, runs finally blocks while unwinding, and on the main thread ends the process (exit code 101) with the message and a stack trace; in a worker, the parent gets a WorkerPanicked error. For failures a caller should handle, throw an error instead.

items.name: parseFloat
items.doc: The number at the start of s, like JavaScript's parseFloat(s): leading whitespace, then the longest decimal number (or Infinity); NaN without one.

examples.code:
println(parseFloat("3.14 m"))   // 3.14
println(parseFloat("abc"))      // NaN

items.name: parseInt
items.doc: The integer at the start of s, like JavaScript's parseInt(s) in base 10: leading whitespace, an optional sign, then digits up to the first non-digit. Panics without any digits (int has no NaN).

examples.code:
println(parseInt("42"))         // 42
println(parseInt("  -7 apples"))   // -7

items.name: print
items.doc:
Writes value's string form to standard output, without a newline.

Anything with a string form can be printed: numbers, bool, char, strings, class instances (their toString(), or Name (field = value, …)) and nullable ones of these (null). For other values, build the text first: print(xs.join(", ")), print(`${p.x}, ${p.y}`).

examples.code:
print("a")
print(1)
println()   // a1

items.name: println
items.doc:
Writes value's string form and a newline to standard output; without an argument, just the newline.

Anything with a string form can be printed: numbers, bool, char, strings, class instances (their toString(), or Name (field = value, …)) and nullable ones of these (null). To print several values, use a template: println(`${a} ${b}`).

examples.code:
println("hello")   // hello
println(42)        // 42
println()          // an empty line

items.name: queueMicrotask
items.doc: Runs f once the current task (and the microtasks before it) has finished.

examples.code:
setTimeout(() => println("timer"), 0)
queueMicrotask(() => println("microtask"))
println("sync")   // sync, then: microtask, timer

items.name: setInterval
items.signature: function setInterval(f: () => void, ms: int = 0): int
items.doc: Calls f every ms milliseconds until cleared.

items.name: setTimeout
items.signature: function setTimeout(f: () => void, ms: int = 0): int
items.doc: Calls f after ms milliseconds (at the earliest); the id cancels it.

examples.code:
setTimeout(() => println("later"), 10)
println("now")   // now, then: later

items.name: watchEffect
items.doc: Runs fn now, and again (synchronously) after every change of the reactive state it read (spec §16.4).

examples.code:
reactive price = 10
reactive qty = 2
watchEffect(() => println(`total: ${price * qty}`))   // total: 20
qty = 3                                               // total: 30

modules.name: String
modules.about: The methods and properties of the built-in String type.

items.name: codePointAt
items.doc: The code point at position i (positions count code points), or null outside the string (#156).

examples.code:
println("A€".codePointAt(1))   // 8364
println("A€".codePointAt(5))   // null

items.name: endsWith
items.doc: Whether the string ends with suffix.

examples.code: println("main.pi".endsWith(".pi"))   // true

items.name: includes
items.doc: Whether search occurs in the string.

examples.code: println("pico lang".includes("lang"))   // true

items.name: indexOf
items.doc: Where the first occurrence of search starts (in code points, like s[i]), or -1. An empty search is found at 0.

examples.code:
println("hello".indexOf("l"))   // 2
println("hello".indexOf("z"))   // -1

items.name: lastIndexOf
items.doc: The last position of search in s, or -1.

examples.code:
println("a/b/c".lastIndexOf("/"))   // 3
println("a/b/c".lastIndexOf("x"))   // -1

items.name: length
items.doc: How many code points the string has (as s[i] and the string methods count).

examples.code: println("héllo".length)   // 5

items.name: localeCompare
items.doc: Compares s with other for sorting text (#156): ignoring case first, then lower case before upper case, as ICU's root collation orders ASCII (JavaScript's localeCompare). Negative, 0 or positive.

examples.code:
const names = ["bob", "Alice", "carol"]
names.sort((a, b) => a.localeCompare(b))
println(names.join(", "))   // Alice, bob, carol

items.name: match
items.doc: The first match of re (no g flag), or every match's text (g); null without one.

items.name: matchAll
items.doc: Every match of re, with its groups and index.

items.name: padEnd
items.doc: The string padded with spaces at the end to length code points (unchanged if it's that long already).

examples.code: println(`[${"ab".padEnd(5)}]`)   // [ab   ]

items.name: padEnd
items.doc: The string padded at the end to length code points with fill, repeated and cut to fit (unchanged if it's that long already, or fill is empty).

examples.code: println("ab".padEnd(6, "-="))   // ab-=-=

items.name: padStart
items.doc: The string padded with spaces at the start to length code points (unchanged if it's that long already): "7".padStart(3) is " 7".

examples.code: println(`[${"7".padStart(3)}]`)   // [  7]

items.name: padStart
items.doc: The string padded at the start to length code points with fill, repeated and cut to fit (unchanged if it's that long already, or fill is empty): "7".padStart(3, "0") is "007".

examples.code: println("7".padStart(3, "0"))   // 007

items.name: repeat
items.doc: The string count times over: "ab".repeat(3) is "ababab" (empty for a count of 0 or less).

examples.code: println("ab".repeat(3))   // ababab

items.name: replace
items.signature: replace(search: string | RegExp, replacement: string | ((m: RegExpMatch) => string)): string
items.doc: Replaces the first occurrence of search (every match for a RegExp with the g flag). replacement may use $&, $1, $<name>, $`, $' and $$, or be a function of the match.

examples.code:
println("one two two".replace("two", "2"))         // one 2 two
println("a1b22".replace(/\d+/g, "#"))              // a#b#
println("john smith".replace(/(\w+) (\w+)/, "$2, $1"))   // smith, john

items.name: replaceAll
items.signature: replaceAll(search: string | RegExp, replacement: string | ((m: RegExpMatch) => string)): string
items.doc: Replaces every occurrence of search (a RegExp needs the g flag).

examples.code:
println("one two two".replaceAll("two", "2"))   // one 2 2
println("a-b_c".replaceAll(/[-_]/g, (m) => "."))   // a.b.c

items.name: search
items.doc: Where the first match of re starts, or -1.

examples.code: println("abc123".search(/\d/))   // 3

items.name: slice
items.doc: The part of the string from code point start up to (not including) end, or to the end. Negative indices count from the end; both are clamped to the string.

examples.code:
const s = "pico-lang"
println(s.slice(0, 4))   // pico
println(s.slice(-4))     // lang

items.name: split
items.signature: split(separator: string | RegExp, limit: int = -1): string[]
items.doc: The pieces of the string between occurrences of separator (a string or a RegExp, whose captured groups are spliced in), at most limit of them; an empty separator splits into characters.

examples.code:
println("a,b,c".split(",").join(" | "))      // a | b | c
println("a,b,c".split(",", 2).join(" | "))   // a | b
println("1 + 2".split(/\s*\+\s*/).join(" | "))   // 1 | 2

items.name: startsWith
items.doc: Whether the string starts with prefix.

examples.code: println("main.pi".startsWith("main"))   // true

items.name: substring
items.signature: substring(start: int, end: int = s.length): string
items.doc: The text from start up to end (default: the end), as JavaScript's substring (#156): both are clamped to the string, and swapped when start is greater.

examples.code:
println("Hello, world".substring(7))      // world
println("Hello, world".substring(5, 0))   // Hello

items.name: toLowerCase
items.doc: ASCII letters only.

examples.code: println("Hello, World".toLowerCase())   // hello, world

items.name: toUpperCase
items.doc: ASCII letters only.

examples.code: println("Hello, world".toUpperCase())   // HELLO, WORLD

items.name: trim
items.doc: The string without leading and trailing whitespace (spaces, tabs, line breaks, vertical tabs and form feeds).

examples.code: println(`[${"\t hi \n".trim()}]`)   // [hi]

items.name: trimEnd
items.doc: The string without trailing whitespace (spaces, tabs, line breaks, vertical tabs and form feeds).

examples.code: println(`[${"  hi  ".trimEnd()}]`)   // [  hi]

items.name: trimStart
items.doc: The string without leading whitespace (spaces, tabs, line breaks, vertical tabs and form feeds).

examples.code: println(`[${"  hi  ".trimStart()}]`)   // [hi  ]

modules.name: Array
modules.about: The methods and properties of the built-in Array type.

items.name: concat
items.doc: A new array of this array's elements followed by other's.

items.name: every
items.signature: every<T, E extends Error>(f: (x: T) => bool throws E): bool throws E
items.doc: Whether f is true for every element (stops at the first that isn't; true for an empty array).

examples.code: println([2, 4, 6].every((x) => x % 2 == 0))   // true

items.name: filter
items.signature: filter<T, E extends Error>(f: (x: T) => bool throws E): T[] throws E
items.doc: A new array of the elements for which f is true, in order.

examples.code:
const evens = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5].filter((x) => x % 2 == 0)
println(evens.join(", "))   // 2, 4

items.name: find
items.signature: find<T, E extends Error>(f: (x: T) => bool throws E): T? throws E
items.doc: The first element for which f is true, or null.

examples.code:
const words = ["pear", "apple", "plum"]
println(words.find((w) => w.startsWith("p")))   // pear
println(words.find((w) => w.length > 9))        // null

items.name: findIndex
items.signature: findIndex<T, E extends Error>(f: (x: T) => bool throws E): int throws E
items.doc: The index of the first element for which f is true, or -1.

examples.code:
const xs = [3, 8, 12]
println(xs.findIndex((x) => x > 5))    // 1
println(xs.findIndex((x) => x > 50))   // -1

items.name: forEach
items.signature: forEach<T, E extends Error>(f: (x: T) => void throws E): void throws E
items.doc: Calls f with each element, in order.

items.name: includes
items.doc: Whether an element is == value.

examples.code: println([1, 2, 3].includes(2))   // true

items.name: indexOf
items.doc: The index of the first element == value, or -1.

examples.code:
const xs = ["a", "b", "c"]
println(xs.indexOf("c"))   // 2
println(xs.indexOf("z"))   // -1

items.name: iterator
items.doc: The elements of an array, lazily (xs.iterator()).

items.name: join
items.doc: The elements' string forms joined with commas: [1, 2].join() is "1,2".

items.name: join
items.doc: The elements' string forms joined with separator: ["a", "b"].join(", ") is "a, b".

examples.code: println(["a", "b", "c"].join(" - "))   // a - b - c

items.name: length
items.doc: How many elements the array has.

examples.code:
const xs = [1, 2, 3]
println(xs.length)   // 3

items.name: map
items.signature: map<T, U, E extends Error>(f: (x: T) => U throws E): U[] throws E
items.doc: A new array of f of each element, in order: [1, 2].map(x => x * 2) is [2, 4].

examples.code:
const doubled = [1, 2, 3].map((x) => x * 2)
println(doubled.join(", "))   // 2, 4, 6

items.name: pop
items.doc: Removes the last element and returns it; null (and nothing changes) when the array is empty.

examples.code:
const xs = [1, 2]
println(xs.pop())     // 2
println(xs.length)    // 1

items.name: push
items.doc: Appends values to the end of the array, in order.

examples.code:
const xs: int[] = []
xs.push(1)
xs.push(2, 3)
println(xs.join(", "))   // 1, 2, 3

items.name: reduce
items.signature: reduce<T, A, E extends Error>(f: (acc: A, x: T) => A throws E, initial: A, ): A throws E
items.doc: Folds the elements into one value: f(acc, x) for each element in order, starting from initial. [1, 2, 3].reduce((sum, x) => sum + x, 0) is 6.

examples.code:
const total = [1, 2, 3].reduce((sum, x) => sum + x, 0)
println(total)   // 6

items.name: reverse
items.doc: Reverses in place and returns the array.

examples.code:
const xs = [1, 2, 3]
xs.reverse()
println(xs.join(","))   // 3,2,1

items.name: shift
items.doc: Removes the first element and returns it; null (and nothing changes) when the array is empty (#156).

examples.code:
const queue = ["a", "b"]
println(queue.shift())   // a
println(queue.length)    // 1

items.name: slice
items.doc: A new array of the elements from index start to the end. A negative start counts from the end (xs.slice(-2): the last two); it's clamped to the array.

examples.code:
const xs = [1, 2, 3, 4]
println(xs.slice(1).join(","))    // 2,3,4
println(xs.slice(-2).join(","))   // 3,4

items.name: slice
items.doc: A new array of the elements from index start up to (not including) end. Negative indices count from the end; both are clamped to the array, and start >= end gives an empty array.

examples.code:
const xs = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
println(xs.slice(1, 3).join(","))    // 2,3
println(xs.slice(0, -1).join(","))   // 1,2,3,4

items.name: some
items.signature: some<T, E extends Error>(f: (x: T) => bool throws E): bool throws E
items.doc: Whether f is true for at least one element (stops at the first; false for an empty array).

examples.code: println([1, 3, 4].some((x) => x % 2 == 0))   // true

items.name: sort
items.doc: Sorts in place (stable merge sort) by < and returns the array.

examples.code:
const xs = [3, 1, 2]
xs.sort()
println(xs.join(","))   // 1,2,3

items.name: sort
items.signature: sort<T, E extends Error>(compare: (a: T, b: T) => int throws E): T[] throws E
items.doc: Sorts in place (stable merge sort) by compare (negative: a first) and returns the array.

examples.code:
const words = ["kiwi", "fig", "banana"]
words.sort((a, b) => a.length - b.length)
println(words.join(","))   // fig,kiwi,banana

items.name: splice
items.doc: Removes the elements from index start to the end (in place) and returns them. A negative start counts from the end; it's clamped to the array.

examples.code:
const xs = [1, 2, 3, 4]
const tail = xs.splice(2)
println(xs.join(","))     // 1,2
println(tail.join(","))   // 3,4

items.name: splice
items.signature: splice<T>(start: int, deleteCount: int, ...items: T[]): T[]
items.doc: Removes deleteCount elements from index start, inserts items there (in place), and returns the removed elements. A negative start counts from the end; start and the count are clamped to the array.

examples.code:
const xs = ["a", "b", "c", "d"]
const removed = xs.splice(1, 2, "X")
println(xs.join(","))        // a,X,d
println(removed.join(","))   // b,c

items.name: sum
items.doc: The sum of the elements (0 for none).

examples.code: println([1, 2, 3].sum())   // 6

items.name: unshift
items.doc: Inserts items at the start; the new length (#156).

examples.code:
const xs = [3, 4]
println(xs.unshift(1, 2))   // 4
println(xs.join(","))       // 1,2,3,4

modules.name: std/bytes
modules.about: std/bytes (spec §13.5): ByteBuffer, a growable run of bytes that is written at its end and read from its front, like Go's bytes.Buffer: an encoder's output, or a parser's input that arrives in chunks.

items.name: ByteBuffer
items.doc: Bytes written at the end (write, writeByte, the DataView-style writeUint16 …) and read from the front (read, skip, get). The storage grows by doubling; bytes already read are reclaimed when more room is needed, so a long-lived buffer stays as large as what it holds.

examples.code:
import { ByteBuffer } from "std/bytes"

const buf = new ByteBuffer()
buf.writeByte(1)
buf.writeUint16(500)
const kind = buf.read(1)
if (kind != null) println(kind.get(0))   // 1
println(buf.length)                      // 2

members.name: constructor
members.doc: An empty buffer with room for capacity bytes before it first grows.

members.name: length
members.doc: How many bytes it holds (written and not read yet).

examples.code:
import { ByteBuffer } from "std/bytes"

const buf = new ByteBuffer()
buf.write(new TextEncoder().encode("abc"))
println(buf.length)   // 3
buf.skip(1)
println(buf.length)   // 2

members.name: get
members.doc: The byte at i of the ones it holds; panics outside 0..length.

examples.code:
import { ByteBuffer } from "std/bytes"

const buf = new ByteBuffer()
buf.write(new TextEncoder().encode("hi!"))
println(buf.get(0))   // 104
println(buf.get(2))   // 33

members.name: bytes
members.doc: The bytes it holds, without a copy: the view is valid until the next write.

examples.code:
import { ByteBuffer } from "std/bytes"

const buf = new ByteBuffer()
buf.write(new TextEncoder().encode("hello"))
println(new TextDecoder().decode(buf.bytes()))   // hello

members.name: toUint8Array
members.doc: A copy of the bytes it holds.

members.name: reserve
members.doc: Makes room for n more bytes at the end.

members.name: write
members.doc: Appends bytes.

examples.code:
import { ByteBuffer } from "std/bytes"

const buf = new ByteBuffer()
buf.write(new TextEncoder().encode("foo"))
buf.write(new TextEncoder().encode("bar"))
println(new TextDecoder().decode(buf.bytes()))   // foobar

members.name: writeByte
members.doc: Appends one byte (b's low 8 bits).

examples.code:
import { ByteBuffer } from "std/bytes"

const buf = new ByteBuffer()
buf.writeByte(0x41)
buf.writeByte(0x142)   // only the low 8 bits: 0x42
println(new TextDecoder().decode(buf.bytes()))   // AB

members.name: writeUint16
members.signature: public writeUint16(value: int, littleEndian: bool = false): void
members.doc: Appends value as 2 bytes, big-endian unless littleEndian.

examples.code:
import { ByteBuffer } from "std/bytes"
import { hex } from "std/encoding"

const buf = new ByteBuffer()
buf.writeUint16(0x1234)
buf.writeUint16(0x1234, true)
println(hex.encode(buf.bytes()))   // 12343412

members.name: writeUint32
members.signature: public writeUint32(value: int, littleEndian: bool = false): void
members.doc: Appends value as 4 bytes, big-endian unless littleEndian.

examples.code:
import { ByteBuffer } from "std/bytes"
import { hex } from "std/encoding"

const buf = new ByteBuffer()
buf.writeUint32(0xCAFE)
println(hex.encode(buf.bytes()))   // 0000cafe

members.name: writeBigUint64
members.signature: public writeBigUint64(value: u64, littleEndian: bool = false): void
members.doc: Appends value as 8 bytes, big-endian unless littleEndian.

examples.code:
import { ByteBuffer } from "std/bytes"
import { hex } from "std/encoding"

const buf = new ByteBuffer()
buf.writeBigUint64(258, true)
println(hex.encode(buf.bytes()))   // 0201000000000000

members.name: writeFloat16
members.signature: public writeFloat16(value: f64, littleEndian: bool = false): void
members.doc: Appends value as a 2-byte half-precision float, big-endian unless littleEndian.

examples.code:
import { ByteBuffer } from "std/bytes"
import { hex } from "std/encoding"

const buf = new ByteBuffer()
buf.writeFloat16(1.5)
println(hex.encode(buf.bytes()))   // 3e00

members.name: writeFloat32
members.signature: public writeFloat32(value: f32, littleEndian: bool = false): void
members.doc: Appends value as a 4-byte float, big-endian unless littleEndian.

examples.code:
import { ByteBuffer } from "std/bytes"
import { hex } from "std/encoding"

const buf = new ByteBuffer()
buf.writeFloat32(1.5)
println(hex.encode(buf.bytes()))   // 3fc00000

members.name: writeFloat64
members.signature: public writeFloat64(value: f64, littleEndian: bool = false): void
members.doc: Appends value as an 8-byte float, big-endian unless littleEndian.

examples.code:
import { ByteBuffer } from "std/bytes"
import { hex } from "std/encoding"

const buf = new ByteBuffer()
buf.writeFloat64(1.5, true)
println(hex.encode(buf.bytes()))   // 000000000000f83f

members.name: read
members.doc: A copy of the next n bytes, which are then read; null (and nothing read) while it holds fewer.

examples.code:
import { ByteBuffer } from "std/bytes"

const buf = new ByteBuffer()
buf.write(new TextEncoder().encode("GET /"))
const verb = buf.read(3)
if (verb != null) println(new TextDecoder().decode(verb))   // GET
println(buf.read(10) == null)                               // true
println(buf.length)                                         // 2

members.name: skip
members.doc: Drops the next n bytes (all of them if it holds fewer).

examples.code:
import { ByteBuffer } from "std/bytes"

const buf = new ByteBuffer()
buf.write(new TextEncoder().encode("header:body"))
buf.skip(7)
println(new TextDecoder().decode(buf.bytes()))   // body

members.name: clear
members.doc: Drops everything it holds (keeping the storage).

examples.code:
import { ByteBuffer } from "std/bytes"

const buf = new ByteBuffer()
buf.write(new TextEncoder().encode("abc"))
buf.clear()
println(buf.length)   // 0

modules.name: std/checksum
modules.about: std/checksum (spec §13.5): cyclic redundancy checks of any width up to 32 bits, described the way the CRC catalogue (reveng) does: polynomial, initial value, whether bytes go in least significant bit first ("reflected"), and what the result is XORed with. Table-driven, with a table per polynomial, made on first use.

items.name: CrcSpec
items.doc: A CRC algorithm. poly is the polynomial without its top bit, written most significant bit first (CRC-32's is 0x04C11DB7) whether or not the CRC is reflected.

members.name: width
members.doc: Bits: 8 to 32.

members.name: init
members.doc: The register's value before the first byte.

members.name: reflected
members.doc: Whether bytes go in least significant bit first (and the result comes out that way).

members.name: xorOut
members.doc: XORed with the register to give the result.

items.name: CRC32
items.doc: CRC-32 (ISO-HDLC): zlib's, PNG's, Ethernet's. Check value (of "123456789"): 0xCBF43926.

items.name: CRC32C
items.doc: CRC-32C (Castagnoli: iSCSI, ext4, SCTP). Check: 0xE3069283.

items.name: CRC16_MCRF4XX
items.doc: CRC-16/MCRF4XX: MAVLink's checksum (often called "X.25 CRC", though X.25 also inverts the result). Check: 0x6F91.

items.name: CRC16_X25
items.doc: CRC-16/IBM-SDLC (X.25, HDLC). Check: 0x906E.

items.name: CRC16_CCITT_FALSE
items.doc: CRC-16/IBM-3740 ("CCITT-FALSE"). Check: 0x29B1.

items.name: CRC16_XMODEM
items.doc: CRC-16/XMODEM. Check: 0x31C3.

items.name: CRC16_KERMIT
items.doc: CRC-16/KERMIT. Check: 0x2189.

items.name: CRC16_MODBUS
items.doc: CRC-16/MODBUS. Check: 0x4B37.

items.name: CRC16_ARC
items.doc: CRC-16/ARC (LHA). Check: 0xBB3D.

items.name: CRC8
items.doc: CRC-8/SMBUS. Check: 0xF4.

items.name: Crc
items.doc:
A running CRC: update it with bytes as they come, read value at any point.

const c = new Crc(CRC16_MCRF4XX).update(header).updateByte(crcExtra)

examples.code:
import { Crc, CRC16_MCRF4XX } from "std/checksum"

const c = new Crc(CRC16_MCRF4XX)
c.update(new TextEncoder().encode("12345"))
c.update(new TextEncoder().encode("6789"))
println(`${c.value:#X}`)   // 0x6F91

members.name: constructor
members.doc: A CRC of no bytes yet; or, with previous, carrying on after bytes whose CRC was previous (crc(b, spec, crc(a, spec)) is the CRC of a then b).

examples.code:
import { Crc, CRC32, crc32 } from "std/checksum"

const first = crc32(new TextEncoder().encode("12345"))
const c = new Crc(CRC32, first)   // carries on after "12345"
c.update(new TextEncoder().encode("6789"))
println(`${c.value:#X}`)   // 0xCBF43926

members.name: update
members.doc: Takes bytes in.

members.name: updateByte
members.doc: Takes one byte (b's low 8 bits) in.

members.name: value
members.doc: The CRC of the bytes so far.

examples.code:
import { Crc, CRC32 } from "std/checksum"

const c = new Crc(CRC32)
println(c.value)   // 0
c.update(new TextEncoder().encode("123456789"))
println(`${c.value:#X}`)   // 0xCBF43926

members.name: reset
members.doc: Starts again with no bytes.

examples.code:
import { Crc, CRC16_XMODEM } from "std/checksum"

const c = new Crc(CRC16_XMODEM).update(new TextEncoder().encode("junk"))
c.reset()
c.update(new TextEncoder().encode("123456789"))
println(`${c.value:#X}`)   // 0x31C3

items.name: crc
items.signature: function crc(bytes: Uint8Array, spec: CrcSpec = CRC32, previous: int? = null): int
items.doc: The CRC of bytes (by default CRC-32), carrying on from previous if given.

examples.code:
import { crc, CRC16_MODBUS, CRC8 } from "std/checksum"

const data = new TextEncoder().encode("123456789")
println(`${crc(data):#X}`)                 // 0xCBF43926
println(`${crc(data, CRC16_MODBUS):#X}`)   // 0x4B37
println(`${crc(data, CRC8):#X}`)           // 0xF4

items.name: crc32
items.signature: function crc32(bytes: Uint8Array, previous: int = 0): int
items.doc: zlib's crc32(previous, bytes): CRC-32 of bytes, carrying on from previous (0: none).

modules.name: std/collections
modules.about:
std/collections (spec §13.2): Deque (a double-ended queue), PriorityQueue (a binary heap), SortedMap (keys kept in order) and BitSet. Each one walks with for-of.

Iterators end at null (spec §5.7), so iterating a collection of a nullable type stops at its first null element; use toArray() for those.

items.name: Deque
items.doc: A double-ended queue: push and pop at both ends in amortized O(1), index in O(1).

examples.code:
import { Deque } from "std/collections"

const d = new Deque<int>([2, 3])
d.pushFront(1)
d.pushBack(4)
println(d.popFront())              // 1
println(d.popBack())               // 4
println(d.toArray().join(", "))    // 2, 3

members.name: constructor
members.doc: A deque holding items, front to back.

examples.code:
import { Deque } from "std/collections"

const d = new Deque<string>(["a", "b", "c"])
println(d.peekFront())   // a
println(d.length)        // 3

members.name: length
members.doc: The number of elements.

examples.code:
import { Deque } from "std/collections"

const d = new Deque<int>([1, 2])
d.push(3)
println(d.length)   // 3

members.name: isEmpty
members.doc: Whether there are no elements.

examples.code:
import { Deque } from "std/collections"

const d = new Deque<int>()
println(d.isEmpty)   // true
d.push(1)
println(d.isEmpty)   // false

members.name: pushBack
members.doc: Adds x at the back (also push).

examples.code:
import { Deque } from "std/collections"

const d = new Deque<int>([1])
d.pushBack(2)
println(d.peekBack())   // 2

members.name: push
members.doc: Adds x at the back (the same as pushBack).

examples.code:
import { Deque } from "std/collections"

const d = new Deque<int>()
d.push(1)
d.push(2)
println(d.toArray().join(", "))   // 1, 2

members.name: pushFront
members.doc: Adds x at the front (also unshift).

examples.code:
import { Deque } from "std/collections"

const d = new Deque<int>([2])
d.pushFront(1)
println(d.peekFront())   // 1

members.name: unshift
members.doc: Adds x at the front (the same as pushFront).

examples.code:
import { Deque } from "std/collections"

const d = new Deque<int>([3])
d.unshift(2)
d.unshift(1)
println(d.toArray().join(", "))   // 1, 2, 3

members.name: popBack
members.doc: Removes and returns the last element (null when empty; also pop).

examples.code:
import { Deque } from "std/collections"

const d = new Deque<int>([1, 2])
println(d.popBack())   // 2
println(d.popBack())   // 1
println(d.popBack())   // null

members.name: pop
members.doc: Removes and returns the last element, or null when empty (the same as popBack).

examples.code:
import { Deque } from "std/collections"

const stack = new Deque<string>()
stack.push("a")
stack.push("b")
println(stack.pop())   // b

members.name: popFront
members.doc: Removes and returns the first element (null when empty; also shift).

examples.code:
import { Deque } from "std/collections"

const d = new Deque<int>([1, 2])
println(d.popFront())   // 1
println(d.length)       // 1

members.name: shift
members.doc: Removes and returns the first element, or null when empty (the same as popFront).

examples.code:
import { Deque } from "std/collections"

const queue = new Deque<string>()
queue.push("first")
queue.push("second")
println(queue.shift())   // first

members.name: at
members.doc: The element at i (negative counts from the back), or null out of range.

examples.code:
import { Deque } from "std/collections"

const d = new Deque<string>(["a", "b", "c"])
println(d.at(1))    // b
println(d.at(-1))   // c
println(d.at(5))    // null

members.name: peekFront
members.doc: The first element without removing it, or null when empty.

examples.code:
import { Deque } from "std/collections"

const d = new Deque<int>([7, 8])
println(d.peekFront())   // 7
println(d.length)        // 2

members.name: peekBack
members.doc: The last element without removing it, or null when empty.

members.name: clear
members.doc: Removes every element.

examples.code:
import { Deque } from "std/collections"

const d = new Deque<int>([1, 2, 3])
d.clear()

modules.name: std/crypto
modules.about: std/crypto (spec §13.2): synchronous cryptography over Mbed TLS: hashes, HMAC, HKDF, PBKDF2, AEAD (AES-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305), elliptic-curve keys (P-256, P-384, X25519), ECDSA and ECDH; streaming hashes (createHash). The crypto global has Web Crypto's async subtle over the same code. Strings are taken as their UTF-8 bytes.

import { hex } from "std/encoding"

items.signature: function hkdf(algorithm: HashAlgorithm, ikm: Uint8Array, salt: Uint8Array, info: Uint8Array, length: int): Uint8Array throws CryptoError
items.doc: HKDF (RFC 5869): length bytes from input keying material.

items.name: pbkdf2
items.signature: function pbkdf2(algorithm: HashAlgorithm, password: Uint8Array | string, salt: Uint8Array, iterations: int, length: int): Uint8Array throws CryptoError
items.doc: PBKDF2 with HMAC (RFC 8018): length bytes from a password.

items.name: timingSafeEqual
items.signature: function timingSafeEqual(a: Uint8Array, b: Uint8Array): bool
items.doc: Whether two byte strings are equal, in time that depends only on their length.

items.name: randomBytes
items.doc: n random bytes from the system.

examples.code:
import { randomBytes } from "std/crypto"
import { hex } from "std/encoding"

const nonce = randomBytes(12)
println(nonce.length)       // 12
println(hex.encode(nonce))  // e.g. 9f3c0a… (different every run)

items.name: Aead
items.doc: An AEAD cipher with its key: seal encrypts and authenticates (the result is the ciphertext then a 16-byte tag), open checks and decrypts. Never reuse a nonce with the same key.

members.name: constructor
members.doc: Use Aead.aesGcm(key) or Aead.chacha20Poly1305(key), which check the key (alg: 1 AES-GCM, 2 ChaCha20-Poly1305).

members.name: aesGcm
members.signature: public static aesGcm(key: Uint8Array): Aead throws CryptoError
members.doc: AES-GCM with a 16-, 24- or 32-byte key (nonces: 12 bytes are standard).

members.name: chacha20Poly1305
members.signature: public static chacha20Poly1305(key: Uint8Array): Aead throws CryptoError
members.doc: ChaCha20-Poly1305 (RFC 8439) with a 32-byte key and 12-byte nonces.

members.name: seal
members.signature: public seal(nonce: Uint8Array, plaintext: Uint8Array | string, aad: Uint8Array = new Uint8Array(0)): Uint8Array throws CryptoError
members.doc: The ciphertext of plaintext (a string is its UTF-8 bytes) followed by a 16-byte tag, authenticating aad too. nonce must be unique per key: 12 bytes is standard (and the only size ChaCha20-Poly1305 takes); a nonce of the wrong size throws CryptoError.

members.name: open
members.signature: public open(nonce: Uint8Array, sealed: Uint8Array, aad: Uint8Array = new Uint8Array(0)): Uint8Array throws CryptoError
members.doc: The plaintext; throws CryptoError (AuthenticationFailed) when the data, nonce, associated data or key don't match.

items.name: EcKeyPair
items.doc: An elliptic-curve key pair: the private key (a big-endian scalar; for X25519 the 32-byte RFC 7748 form) and the public key (an uncompressed point 04 ‖ x ‖ y; for X25519 32 bytes).

members.name: curve
members.doc: The curve both keys belong to.

members.name: privateKey
members.doc: The private key: a big-endian scalar (for X25519, the 32-byte RFC 7748 form). Keep it secret.

members.name: publicKey
members.doc: The public key: an uncompressed point 04 ‖ x ‖ y (for X25519, 32 bytes).

members.name: constructor
members.signature: constructor(curve: NamedCurve, privateKey: Uint8Array, publicKey: Uint8Array)
members.doc: A pair from its parts (not checked to match); a new one comes from the curve's key generation.

members.name: generate
members.doc: A new random key pair.

examples.code:
import { EcKeyPair } from "std/crypto"

const keys = EcKeyPair.generate("P-384")
println(keys.privateKey.length)   // 48
println(keys.publicKey.length)    // 97

members.name: fromPrivateKey
members.signature: public static fromPrivateKey(curve: NamedCurve, privateKey: Uint8Array): EcKeyPair throws CryptoError
members.doc: The key pair of a private key.

members.name: sign
members.signature: public sign(hash: HashAlgorithm, message: Uint8Array | string): Uint8Array throws CryptoError
members.doc: An ECDSA signature of message (hashed with hash): r ‖ s, deterministic (RFC 6979).

members.name: agree
members.signature: public agree(peerPublicKey: Uint8Array): Uint8Array throws CryptoError
members.doc: The ECDH shared secret with a peer's public key.

items.name: ecdsaVerify
items.signature: function ecdsaVerify(curve: NamedCurve, hash: HashAlgorithm, publicKey: Uint8Array, message: Uint8Array | string, signature: Uint8Array): bool
items.doc: Whether signature (r ‖ s) is publicKey's ECDSA signature of message.

items.name: CryptoError
items.doc: A failed cryptographic operation: a bad key or argument, or data that doesn't authenticate. kind is "InvalidArgument", "InvalidAccess" (a key used for something its usages don't allow), "AuthenticationFailed" or "Internal".

members.name: kind
members.doc: "InvalidArgument", "InvalidAccess", "AuthenticationFailed" or "Internal".

members.name: constructor
members.doc: An error of kind with message.

items.name: CryptoKey
items.doc: A key for crypto.subtle (Web Crypto): its algorithm, usages and bytes (raw secret bytes, a private scalar, or an uncompressed public point).

members.name: type
members.doc: "secret", "private" or "public".

members.name: extractable
members.doc: Whether exportKey may export a non-public key's bytes.

members.name: algorithm
members.doc: The algorithm the key is for, with its hash, curve or length.

members.name: usages
members.doc: What the key may be used for ("sign", "verify", "encrypt", "decrypt", "deriveBits"): another use rejects with an "InvalidAccess" CryptoError.

members.name: constructor
members.signature: constructor(type: string, extractable: bool, algorithm: KeyAlgorithm, usages: string[], bytes: Uint8Array)
members.doc: A key from its parts; crypto.subtle's generateKey and importKey make them.

items.name: KeyAlgorithm
items.doc: A key's algorithm: name ("HMAC", "AES-GCM", "ECDSA", "ECDH", "HKDF", "PBKDF2"), and its hash, namedCurve or length (bits).

members.name: name
members.doc: The algorithm's name ("HMAC", "AES-GCM", …).

members.name: hash
members.doc: The hash ("SHA-256", …), for HMAC keys.

members.name: namedCurve
members.doc: The curve ("P-256", "P-384", "X25519"), for ECDSA and ECDH keys.

members.name: length
members.doc: The key's length in bits, for secret keys.

items.name: Algorithm
items.doc: Web Crypto algorithm parameters, one struct for all of them (fields as the spec names them): { name: "AES-GCM", iv }, { name: "HMAC", hash: "SHA-256" }, { name: "ECDSA", hash: "SHA-256" }, { name: "ECDSA", namedCurve: "P-256" }, { name: "ECDH", public: key }, { name: "HKDF", hash, salt, info }, { name: "PBKDF2", hash, salt, iterations }, { name: "AES-GCM", length: 256 }.

members.name: name
members.doc: The algorithm's name ("AES-GCM", "HMAC", "ECDSA", "ECDH", "HKDF", "PBKDF2"; any case), or, for digest, the hash's.

members.name: hash
members.doc: The hash ("SHA-256", …) for HMAC, ECDSA, HKDF and PBKDF2. HMAC falls back on the key's.

members.name: namedCurve
members.doc: The curve for generateKey and importKey of ECDSA ("P-256", "P-384") and ECDH keys (also "X25519").

members.name: length
members.doc: The key length in bits for generateKey (AES-GCM: 128, 192 or 256; HMAC: 256 unless given).

members.name: iv
members.doc: AES-GCM's nonce (required; 12 bytes is usual), or AES-CBC's initialization vector (16 bytes).

members.name: counter
members.doc: AES-CTR's initial counter block (16 bytes); length is then how many of its rightmost bits count up (#69).

members.name: additionalData
members.doc: AES-GCM's authenticated, unencrypted data (none unless given).

members.name: tagLength
members.doc: AES-GCM's tag length in bits: only 128 (the default) is supported.

members.name: public
members.doc: ECDH's peer public key, for deriveBits.

members.name: salt
members.doc: The HKDF or PBKDF2 salt (empty unless given).

members.name: info
members.doc: HKDF's context info (empty unless given).

members.name: iterations
members.doc: PBKDF2's iteration count.

items.name: CryptoKeyPair
items.doc: generateKey's result for key-pair algorithms.

members.name: publicKey
members.doc: The public key (always extractable).

members.name: privateKey
members.doc: The private key (extractable as generateKey was told).

items.name: SubtleCrypto
items.doc: Web Crypto's SubtleCrypto (crypto.subtle): digest, generateKey, importKey and exportKey ("raw"), sign/verify (HMAC, ECDSA), encrypt/decrypt (AES-GCM) and deriveBits (ECDH, HKDF, PBKDF2). Results are Uint8Arrays (Web Crypto's are ArrayBuffers); failures reject with CryptoError.

members.name: digest
members.signature: async digest(algorithm: Algorithm | string, data: Uint8Array): Promise<Uint8Array> throws CryptoError
members.doc: The hash of data with algorithm ("SHA-256" or { name: "SHA-256" }; the SHA-1, SHA-2 and SHA-3 hashes).

members.name: importKey
members.signature: async importKey(format: string, keyData: Uint8Array, algorithm: Algorithm | string, extractable: bool, usages: string[]): Promise<CryptoKey> throws CryptoError
members.doc: A key from raw bytes (format must be "raw"): a secret key for HMAC (needs hash), AES-GCM (16, 24 or 32 bytes), HKDF or PBKDF2, or, for ECDSA/ECDH (needs namedCurve), a public key (an uncompressed point on the curve; always extractable).

members.name: exportKey
members.signature: async exportKey(format: string, key: CryptoKey): Promise<Uint8Array> throws CryptoError
members.doc: A copy of key's bytes (format must be "raw"); rejects for a key that is neither extractable nor public.

members.name: generateKey
members.signature: async generateKey(algorithm: Algorithm, extractable: bool, usages: string[]): Promise<CryptoKey | CryptoKeyPair> throws CryptoError
members.doc: A secret key (HMAC, AES-GCM) or, for ECDSA/ECDH, a key pair.

members.name: sign
members.signature: async sign(algorithm: Algorithm | string, key: CryptoKey, data: Uint8Array): Promise<Uint8Array> throws CryptoError
members.doc: An HMAC tag, or an ECDSA signature (r ‖ s, as Web Crypto gives it).

members.name: verify
members.signature: async verify(algorithm: Algorithm | string, key: CryptoKey, signature: Uint8Array, data: Uint8Array): Promise<bool> throws CryptoError
members.doc: Whether signature is data's HMAC tag (compared in constant time) or its ECDSA signature (r ‖ s, with a public key).

members.name: encrypt
members.signature: async encrypt(algorithm: Algorithm, key: CryptoKey, data: Uint8Array): Promise<Uint8Array> throws CryptoError
members.doc: AES-GCM ({ name: "AES-GCM", iv, additionalData? }): ciphertext ‖ 16-byte tag.

members.name: decrypt
members.signature: async decrypt(algorithm: Algorithm, key: CryptoKey, data: Uint8Array): Promise<Uint8Array> throws CryptoError
members.doc: AES-GCM: the plaintext of data (ciphertext ‖ 16-byte tag); rejects with "AuthenticationFailed" if the key, iv, additionalData or data are wrong.

members.name: deriveBits
members.signature: async deriveBits(algorithm: Algorithm, key: CryptoKey, length: int? = null): Promise<Uint8Array> throws CryptoError
members.doc: length bits from ECDH ({ name: "ECDH", public }, a private key), HKDF or PBKDF2 (a raw key imported for them).

modules.name: std/encoding
modules.about: std/encoding: bytes as text (spec §13.5): base64 (RFC 4648, also the URL-safe alphabet) and hex; and csv (RFC 4180). The classes are in the core library (<core>/encoding.pi).

items.name: base64
items.doc: Base64 (RFC 4648): base64.encode(bytes) and base64.decode(text), the standard or the URL-safe alphabet.

items.name: hex
items.doc: Hexadecimal: hex.encode(bytes) (lowercase) and hex.decode(text).

items.name: CsvOptions
items.doc: csv.parse options.

examples.code:
import { csv } from "std/encoding"

println(csv.parse("a;b", { separator: ";" })[0].length)   // 2

members.name: separator
members.doc: The field separator, one character ("," by default).

items.name: CsvWriteOptions
items.doc: csv.stringify options.

examples.code:
import { csv } from "std/encoding"

print(csv.stringify([["a", "b"]], { separator: "\t", lineEnding: "\r\n" }))   // a	b (and CRLF)

members.name: separator
members.doc: The field separator, one character ("," by default).

members.name: lineEnding
members.doc: What ends each row ("\n" by default; RFC 4180 says "\r\n").

items.name: Csv
items.doc: Comma-separated values (RFC 4180; #63): csv.parse(text) into rows of fields, and csv.stringify(rows).

examples.code:
import { csv } from "std/encoding"

const rows = csv.parse("name,note\nAda,\"likes \"\"math\"\", tea\"\n")
println(rows[1][1])            // likes "math", tea
print(csv.stringify(rows))     // name,note / Ada,"likes ""math"", tea"

members.name: constructor
members.doc: A CSV codec (std/encoding exports one as csv).

examples.code:
import { Csv } from "std/encoding"

println(new Csv().parse("x,y").length)   // 1

members.name: parse
members.signature: public parse(text: string, options: CsvOptions = {}): string[][] throws SyntaxError
members.doc: The rows of text: fields split at the separator, rows at line ends (\n or \r\n), a quoted field ("a, ""b""") taking separators, quotes (doubled) and line ends; a last line end ends the last row. A quote inside an unquoted field is kept. Throws a SyntaxError for a quoted field that isn't closed, or text after its closing quote.

members.name: stringify
members.signature: public stringify(rows: string[][], options: CsvWriteOptions = {}): string
members.doc: rows as CSV text: fields joined by the separator, each row ended by the line ending; a field with the separator, a quote, a line end or leading or trailing spaces is quoted (its quotes doubled).

items.name: csv
items.doc: CSV (RFC 4180): csv.parse(text) and csv.stringify(rows).

items.name: Base64
items.doc: Base64 (RFC 4648 §4, or §5's URL-safe alphabet with url).

members.name: constructor
members.doc: A base64 codec (std/encoding exports one as base64).

examples.code:
const b64 = new Base64()
println(b64.encode(Uint8Array.from([1, 2, 3])))   // AQID

members.name: encode
members.signature: public encode(data: Uint8Array, url: bool = false): string
members.doc: data as base64; url uses - and _ and leaves out the = padding.

members.name: decode
members.signature: public decode(text: string): Uint8Array throws TypeError
members.doc: The bytes of base64 text (either alphabet, padding optional; whitespace is skipped). Other characters, or a length no encoding has, throw a TypeError.

items.name: Hex
items.doc: Hexadecimal: two lowercase digits per byte.

examples.code:
import { hex } from "std/encoding"

println(hex.encode(Uint8Array.from([0, 15, 255])))   // 000fff
println(hex.decode("CAFE").get(0))                    // 202

members.name: constructor
members.doc: A hex codec (std/encoding exports one as hex).

examples.code:
const h = new Hex()
println(h.encode(new TextEncoder().encode("A")))   // 41

members.name: encode
members.doc: data as hexadecimal text: two lowercase digits per byte.

examples.code:
const h = new Hex()
println(h.encode(Uint8Array.from([0xDE, 0xAD, 0xBE, 0xEF])))   // deadbeef

members.name: decode
members.signature: public decode(text: string): Uint8Array throws TypeError
members.doc: The bytes of text (digits in either case); an odd length or another character throws a TypeError.

modules.name: std/fmt
modules.about:
std/fmt (spec §1.4, §13.2): the format-spec mini-language at run time, for Formattable types that delegate to their fields (${p:.2f} → formatNumber(x, spec)), and padding and number helpers.

FormatSpec.parse("08.2f") reads [[fill] align] [sign] ["#"] ["0"] [width] ["." precision] [type]; formatInt, formatNumber, formatString and formatBool apply a spec as a template would (floats go through the compiler's own formatting, so rounding is the same: half to even on the exact binary value; precisions up to 20).

items.name: FormatSpec
items.doc: A parsed format spec.

members.name: fill
members.doc: The padding character (a space by default).

members.name: align
members.doc: <, >, ^, or "" (the type's default: numbers right, text left).

members.name: sign
members.doc: - (only negatives), + or .

members.name: alternate
members.doc: #: 0x/0o/0b prefixes.

members.name: zero
members.doc: 0: pad numbers with zeros after the sign (and prefix).

members.name: width
members.doc: -1 when not given.

members.name: precision
members.doc: Digits after the point for floats, or the maximum length for strings; -1 when not given.

members.name: kind
members.doc: One of d x X o b e E f % ?, or "".

members.name: constructor
members.doc: An empty spec (as FormatSpec.parse("")): no width, default alignment and sign.

examples.code:
import { FormatSpec } from "std/fmt"

const spec = new FormatSpec()
spec.width = 6
println(`[${spec.pad("ab", false)}]`)   // [ab    ]

members.name: parse
members.doc: The spec, or null when spec doesn't follow the grammar.

examples.code:
import { FormatSpec } from "std/fmt"

const spec = FormatSpec.parse("+08.3f")
if (spec != null) println(`${spec.sign} ${spec.zero} ${spec.width} ${spec.precision}`)   // + true 8 3
println(FormatSpec.parse("10.2z") == null)                                               // true

members.name: pad
members.signature: public pad(text: string, numeric: bool, prefixLen: int = 0): string
members.doc: Pads text to the width: numeric text aligns right by default and takes 0 padding after its sign and prefix (the sign and prefix are already in text).

examples.code:
import { FormatSpec } from "std/fmt"

const spec = new FormatSpec()
spec.width = 6
println(`[${spec.pad("42", true)}]`)       // [    42]
spec.zero = true
println(`[${spec.pad("-42", true, 1)}]`)   // [-00042]

items.name: formatInt
items.signature: function formatInt(n: int, spec: string = ""): string
items.doc: An integer formatted with spec (d x X o b, or a float type: e E f %).

examples.code:
import { formatInt } from "std/fmt"

println(formatInt(255, "#06x"))   // 0x00ff
println(formatInt(5, "08b"))      // 00000101
println(formatInt(42, "+"))       // +42

items.name: formatNumber
items.signature: function formatNumber(x: number, spec: string = ""): string
items.doc: A number formatted with spec (e E f %, or none: the shortest round-trip form).

examples.code:
import { formatNumber } from "std/fmt"

println(formatNumber(3.14159, ".2f"))   // 3.14
println(formatNumber(0.256, ".1%"))     // 25.6%
println(formatNumber(1234.5, ".1e"))    // 1.2e3

items.name: formatString
items.signature: function formatString(s: string, spec: string = ""): string
items.doc: A string formatted with spec (a precision truncates; ? quotes it).

examples.code:
import { formatString } from "std/fmt"

println(`[${formatString("pico", "^8")}]`)    // [  pico  ]
println(formatString("hello world", ".5"))    // hello
println(formatString("hi", "?"))              // "hi"

items.name: formatBool
items.signature: function formatBool(b: bool, spec: string = ""): string
items.doc: true or false formatted with spec, as a string (formatString): formatBool(ok, ">6") → true.

examples.code:
import { formatBool } from "std/fmt"

println(`[${formatBool(true, ">6")}]`)   // [  true]

items.name: pad
items.signature: function pad(text: string, width: int, align: string = "<", fill: string = " "): string
items.doc: text padded to width code points: align < (left, the default), > or ^.

examples.code:
import { pad } from "std/fmt"

println(`[${pad("ab", 5)}]`)             // [ab   ]
println(`[${pad("ab", 5, ">")}]`)        // [   ab]
println(`[${pad("ab", 6, "^", "*")}]`)   // [**ab**]

items.name: groupDigits
items.signature: function groupDigits(text: string, separator: string = ",", size: int = 3): string
items.doc: The integer part's digits of a number's text in groups (1234567.5 → 1,234,567.5).

examples.code:
import { groupDigits } from "std/fmt"

println(groupDigits("1234567.5"))        // 1,234,567.5
println(groupDigits("-9876543", " "))    // -9 876 543

items.name: wrap
items.signature: function wrap(text: string, width: int): string
items.doc: text wrapped at spaces to lines of at most width code points (decision 344): its own line breaks are kept, a line's leading spaces stay, the spaces where a line is broken and at its end go, and a word longer than width stays whole on its own line.

items.name: wrap
items.signature: function wrap(text: string, width: int, measure: (s: string) => int): string
items.doc: wrap measuring each piece with measure: wrap(text, 60, displayWidth) (std/term) for text with colours or wide characters.

modules.name: std/fs
modules.about: std/fs: the file system (spec §13.2, §13.4). Every operation is async: it runs on the runtime's I/O threads and settles its promise on the event loop. Failures reject with an IoError (a global) naming the path and the kind of failure.

items.name: readText
items.doc: The file's text (UTF-8; anything else rejects with kind "InvalidData").

examples.code:
import { readText, writeText, remove } from "std/fs"
import { tmpDir } from "std/os"
import { join } from "std/path"

const path = join(tmpDir(), "read-text-example.txt")
await writeText(path, "hello\nworld\n")
const text = await readText(path)
println(text.split("\n")[1])   // world
await remove(path)

items.name: readBytes
items.doc: The file's bytes.

examples.code:
import { readBytes, writeText, remove } from "std/fs"
import { tmpDir } from "std/os"
import { join } from "std/path"

const path = join(tmpDir(), "read-bytes-example.txt")
await writeText(path, "AB")
const bytes = await readBytes(path)
println(bytes.length)   // 2
println(bytes[0])       // 65
await remove(path)

items.name: writeText
items.signature: function writeText(path: string, text: string, append: bool = false): Promise<void, IoError>
items.doc: Writes text to the file (created if needed; replaced, or appended to with append).

examples.code:
import { writeText, readText, remove } from "std/fs"
import { tmpDir } from "std/os"
import { join } from "std/path"

const log = join(tmpDir(), "write-text-example.log")
await writeText(log, "first\n")
await writeText(log, "second\n", append: true)
print(await readText(log))   // first, then second
await remove(log)

items.name: writeBytes
items.signature: function writeBytes(path: string, data: Uint8Array, append: bool = false): Promise<void, IoError>
items.doc: Writes the bytes to the file (created if needed; replaced, or appended to with append).

examples.code:
import { writeBytes, readBytes, remove } from "std/fs"
import { tmpDir } from "std/os"
import { join } from "std/path"

const path = join(tmpDir(), "write-bytes-example.bin")
await writeBytes(path, Uint8Array.from([1, 2, 3]))
await writeBytes(path, Uint8Array.from([4]), append: true)
println((await readBytes(path)).length)   // 4
await remove(path)

items.name: FileInfo
items.doc: What stat tells about a path.

examples.code:
import { stat, writeText, remove, FileInfo } from "std/fs"
import { tmpDir } from "std/os"
import { join } from "std/path"

const path = join(tmpDir(), "file-info-example.txt")
await writeText(path, "12345")
const info: FileInfo = await stat(path)
println(info.isFile)        // true
println(info.isDirectory)   // false
println(info.size)          // 5
println(info.mtime)         // when it was written, e.g. 1795430400000
await remove(path)

members.name: isFile
members.doc: Whether it's a regular file.

members.name: isDirectory
members.doc: Whether it's a directory.

members.name: isSymlink
members.doc: Whether it's a symbolic link (only with followLinks: false; otherwise the link's target is described).

members.name: size
members.doc: In bytes.

members.name: mtime
members.doc: The last modification, in milliseconds since 1970 (UTC).

items.name: stat
items.signature: function stat(path: string, followLinks: bool = true): Promise<FileInfo, IoError>
items.doc: Facts about the file or directory at path (following symbolic links unless followLinks is false).

items.name: exists
items.doc: Whether something exists at path.

examples.code:
import { exists, writeText, remove } from "std/fs"
import { tmpDir } from "std/os"
import { join } from "std/path"

const path = join(tmpDir(), "exists-example.txt")
println(await exists(path))   // false
await writeText(path, "")
println(await exists(path))   // true
await remove(path)

items.name: mkdir
items.signature: function mkdir(path: string, recursive: bool = false): Promise<void, IoError>
items.doc: Creates a directory (with recursive, also its missing parents, and an existing directory is fine).

examples.code:
import { mkdir, exists, remove } from "std/fs"
import { tmpDir } from "std/os"
import { join } from "std/path"

const root = join(tmpDir(), "mkdir-example")
await mkdir(join(root, "a", "b"), recursive: true)
println(await exists(join(root, "a", "b")))   // true
await remove(root, recursive: true)

items.name: remove
items.signature: function remove(path: string, recursive: bool = false): Promise<void, IoError>
items.doc: Removes a file or an empty directory (with recursive, a directory and everything in it).

examples.code:
import { mkdir, writeText, remove, exists } from "std/fs"
import { tmpDir } from "std/os"
import { join } from "std/path"

const dir = join(tmpDir(), "remove-example")
await mkdir(dir)
await writeText(join(dir, "a.txt"), "a")
await remove(join(dir, "a.txt"))     // a file
await writeText(join(dir, "b.txt"), "b")
await remove(dir, recursive: true)   // a directory and what's in it
println(await exists(dir))           // false

items.name: rename
items.signature: function rename(from: string, to: string): Promise<void, IoError>
items.doc: Moves or renames from to to (replacing a file there).

examples.code:
import { rename, writeText, readText, remove } from "std/fs"
import { tmpDir } from "std/os"
import { join } from "std/path"

const from = join(tmpDir(), "rename-example.tmp")
const to = join(tmpDir(), "rename-example.txt")
await writeText(from, "moved")
await rename(from, to)
println(await readText(to))   // moved
await remove(to)

items.name: copy
items.signature: function copy(from: string, to: string): Promise<void, IoError>
items.doc: Copies file from to to, replacing a file there; the copy gets from's permissions (#64). A directory rejects (IsADirectory).

examples.code:
import { copy, writeText, readText, remove } from "std/fs"
import { tmpDir } from "std/os"
import { join } from "std/path"

const original = join(tmpDir(), "copy-example.txt")
const backup = join(tmpDir(), "copy-example.bak")
await writeText(original, "keep me")
await copy(original, backup)
println(await readText(backup))   // keep me
await remove(original)
await remove(backup)

items.name: symlink
items.signature: function symlink(target: string, path: string): Promise<void, IoError>
items.doc: Makes path a symbolic link to target (as written: a relative target is relative to the link's directory) (#64). On Windows this needs Developer Mode or the symlink privilege.

examples.code:
import { symlink, readText, writeText, remove, stat } from "std/fs"
import { tmpDir } from "std/os"
import { join } from "std/path"

const target = join(tmpDir(), "symlink-example.txt")
const link = join(tmpDir(), "symlink-example.link")
await writeText(target, "through the link")
await symlink("symlink-example.txt", link)   // relative to the link's directory
println(await readText(link))                // through the link
println((await stat(link, followLinks: false)).isSymlink)   // true
await remove(link)
await remove(target)

items.name: readlink
items.doc: The target of the symbolic link path, as it was written (#64). Not on Windows yet.

examples.code:
import { symlink, readlink, remove } from "std/fs"
import { tmpDir } from "std/os"
import { join } from "std/path"

const link = join(tmpDir(), "readlink-example.link")
await symlink("../somewhere/else", link)
println(await readlink(link))   // ../somewhere/else
await remove(link)

items.name: chmod
items.signature: function chmod(path: string, mode: int): Promise<void, IoError>
items.doc: Sets path's permission bits (0o644, 0o755, …) (#64). On Windows only the owner's write bit counts (the read-only attribute); WASI has no permissions (it rejects).

examples.code:
import { chmod, writeText, remove } from "std/fs"
import { Command } from "std/process"
import { tmpDir } from "std/os"
import { join } from "std/path"

const script = join(tmpDir(), "chmod-example.sh")
await writeText(script, "#!/bin/sh\necho it runs\n")
await chmod(script, 0o755)
println((await new Command(script).output()).stdout.trim())   // it runs
await remove(script)

items.name: DirEntry
items.doc: An entry of a directory.

examples.code:
import { readDir, mkdir, writeText, remove, DirEntry } from "std/fs"
import { tmpDir } from "std/os"
import { join } from "std/path"

const dir = join(tmpDir(), "dir-entry-example")
await mkdir(join(dir, "sub"), recursive: true)
await writeText(join(dir, "a.txt"), "")
for await (const e of readDir(dir)) {
  const entry: DirEntry = e
  println(`${entry.name} ${if (entry.isDirectory) "dir" else "file"}`)   // a.txt file, then sub dir
}
await remove(dir, recursive: true)

members.name: name
members.doc: The entry's name (not a path).

members.name: isFile
members.doc: Whether it's a regular file.

members.name: isDirectory
members.doc: Whether it's a directory.

members.name: isSymlink
members.doc: Whether it's a symbolic link (not followed: a link to a directory is neither isFile nor isDirectory).

items.signature: async function* readDir(path: string): AsyncIterator<DirEntry> throws IoError
items.doc: The entries of a directory (without . and ..), in name order.

examples.code:

const dir = join(tmpDir(), "read-dir-example")

await writeText(join(dir, "b.txt"), "")
await writeText(join(dir, "a.txt"), "")

await remove(dir, recursive: true)

items.name: File
items.doc: An open file: read, write and seek (from the start), then close (or await using).

members.name: path
members.doc: The path the file was opened with.

members.name: constructor
members.doc: Wraps the open descriptor fd; open makes these.

examples.code:

const path = join(tmpDir(), "file-ctor-example.txt")

println(f.path == path)            // true
await f.close()

members.name: read
members.doc: Up to n bytes from the current position; null at the end of the file.

examples.code:
import { open, writeText, remove } from "std/fs"
import { tmpDir } from "std/os"
import { join } from "std/path"

const path = join(tmpDir(), "file-read-example.txt")
await writeText(path, "abcdef")
const f = await open(path)
println((await f.read(4))?.length)   // 4
println((await f.read(4))?.length)   // 2
println(await f.read(4))             // null
await f.close()
await remove(path)

members.name: readable
members.doc: The rest of the file as a stream of chunks (up to 64 KiB each, #64), for files too big to read whole; the file closes when the stream ends or is cancelled. Pipe it through textDecoderStream() (std/streams) for text.

members.name: write
members.doc: Writes all of data at the current position; the count written.

import { join } from "std/path"

const path = join(tmpDir(), "file-write-example.txt")
const f = await open(path, write: true, create: true, truncate: true)
println(await f.write(new TextEncoder().encode("written")))   // 7
await f.close()

members.name: seek
members.doc: Moves to byte position (from the start); the new position.

members.name: close
members.doc: Closes the file (twice is fine: the second call resolves at once). Using it afterwards panics.

examples.code:
import { open, writeText, remove } from "std/fs"
import { tmpDir } from "std/os"
import { join } from "std/path"

const path = join(tmpDir(), "file-close-example.txt")
await writeText(path, "x")
const f = await open(path)
await f.close()
await f.close()   // twice is fine
await remove(path)

members.doc: await using: closes the file, ignoring a failure.

items.name: open
items.signature: function open(path: string, read: bool = true, write: bool = false, append: bool = false, create: bool = false, truncate: bool = false, createNew: bool = false): Promise<File, IoError>
items.doc: Opens a file: for reading by default; write: true to write (with create to create it, truncate to empty it, append to write at its end, createNew to require that it doesn't exist).

examples.code:
import { open, readText, remove } from "std/fs"
import { tmpDir } from "std/os"
import { join } from "std/path"

const path = join(tmpDir(), "open-example.log")
const f = await open(path, write: true, create: true, append: true)
await f.write(new TextEncoder().encode("one line\n"))
await f.close()
print(await readText(path))   // one line
await remove(path)

items.name: WatchEvent
items.doc: A change watch saw: kind is "create", "modify" (a file's size or modification time changed) or "remove"; path is the watched path joined with the changed entry's path (the watched path itself when watching a file). A rename is a remove and a create.

members.name: kind
members.doc: "create", "modify" or "remove".

members.name: path
members.doc: The watched path joined with the changed entry's path (the watched path itself when watching a file).

items.name: Watcher
items.doc: Watches a file or a directory (with recursive, the whole tree below it): an async iterator of WatchEvents, ended by close() (or using). Changes made while nobody waits for an event are compared as a whole when the next one is asked for, so a file created and changed in between is one create, and one created and removed is nothing.

members.name: path
members.doc: The path being watched, as given to watch.

members.name: constructor
members.doc: Wraps the runtime's watch id; watch makes these.

examples.code:
import { watch, Watcher, mkdir, remove } from "std/fs"
import { tmpDir } from "std/os"
import { join } from "std/path"

const dir = join(tmpDir(), "watcher-ctor-example")
await mkdir(dir, recursive: true)
const w: Watcher = await watch(dir)   // `watch` makes Watchers
println(w.path == dir)                // true
w.close()
await remove(dir, recursive: true)

members.name: next
members.doc: The next change (waiting for one), or null once the watcher is closed.

examples.code:
import { watch, writeText, remove, mkdir } from "std/fs"
import { tmpDir } from "std/os"
import { join } from "std/path"

const dir = join(tmpDir(), "watcher-next-example")
await mkdir(dir, recursive: true)
const w = await watch(dir)
const next = w.next()
await writeText(join(dir, "f.txt"), "x")
println((await next)?.kind)   // create
w.close()
println(await w.next() == null)   // true: closed
await remove(dir, recursive: true)

members.name: asyncIterator
members.doc: for await uses the watcher itself.

members.name: close
members.doc: Stops watching: waiting and later next() calls get null. Twice is fine.

members.name: dispose
members.doc: using: the same as close().

items.name: watch
items.signature: function watch(path: string, recursive: bool = true): Promise<Watcher, IoError>
items.doc: Starts watching path (see Watcher); rejects if it can't be looked at.

examples.code:
import { watch, writeText, remove, mkdir } from "std/fs"
import { tmpDir } from "std/os"
import { join } from "std/path"

const dir = join(tmpDir(), "watch-example")
await mkdir(join(dir, "src"), recursive: true)
const w = await watch(dir, recursive: true)
await writeText(join(dir, "src", "main.pi"), "println(1)")
const e = await w.next()
println(e?.kind)   // create
w.close()
await remove(dir, recursive: true)

items.doc: A file read as a ByteStream (std/streams), chunkSize bytes at a time: a recording for protocol code to replay. Writes are discarded, so that code can still answer.

const path = join(tmpDir(), "file-stream-ctor-example.bin")

println((await replay.read())?.length)   // 8
replay.close()

members.signature: public async read(): Promise<Uint8Array?> throws Error

members.name: write
members.signature: public async write(bytes: Uint8Array): Promise<void> throws Error
members.doc: Discards bytes.

examples.code:

members.doc: Stops reading (and closes the file).

const path = join(tmpDir(), "file-stream-close-example.txt")
