modules.name: std/gc
modules.about:
std/gc: controlling the collector (spec §9.2).

import { gc } from "std/gc", then gc.collect(), gc.stats() and so on. The interpreter has no collector of its own: there the calls do nothing and the statistics are zero.

items.name: GcStats
items.doc: A snapshot of the current thread's collector counters (each thread has its own heap). Sizes are in bytes, pauses in nanoseconds; all are 0 in the interpreter.

members.name: heapSize
members.doc: Memory the heap holds from the system (its blocks and large objects).

members.name: usedBytes
members.doc: Bytes in objects that are live or not yet collected.

members.name: allocatedBytes
members.doc: Bytes allocated since the program started (arena allocations included).

members.name: collections
members.doc: Finished full collections (the whole heap): gc.collect() calls and completed incremental cycles.

members.name: youngCollections
members.doc: Nursery-only collections.

members.name: lastPause
members.doc: The most recent pause: an explicit collection, or the collector's work at a safepoint.

members.name: maxPause
members.doc: The longest pause since the start or the last gc.resetStats().

members.name: totalPause
members.doc: All pauses added up since the start or the last gc.resetStats().

items.name: gc
items.doc: The collector's controls, as static methods: gc.collect(), gc.pause(), gc.stats(), …. In the interpreter they do nothing.

examples.code:
import { gc } from "std/gc"

gc.collect()
const s = gc.stats()
println(`${s.collections} collection(s), max pause ${s.maxPause} ns`)   // e.g. 1 collection(s), max pause 458 ns

members.name: collect
members.doc: A full collection now (also while paused); clears every weak reference whose target is unreachable.

examples.code:
import { gc } from "std/gc"

let junk: int[] = []
for (let i = 0; i < 1000; i++) {
  junk = [i, i + 1]
}
gc.collect()
println(gc.stats().collections >= 1)   // true (false in the interpreter)

members.name: collectYoung
members.doc: Collects the nursery only.

examples.code:
import { gc } from "std/gc"

gc.collectYoung()
println(gc.stats().youngCollections >= 1)   // true (false in the interpreter)

members.name: pause
members.doc: No automatic collections until the matching resume() (calls nest). Explicit collect() and collectYoung() still run.

examples.code:
import { gc } from "std/gc"

gc.pause()   // no automatic collections until resume()
let total = 0
for (let i = 0; i < 100; i++) {
  const frame = [i, i * 2, i * 3]
  total += frame[2]
}
gc.resume()
println(total)   // 14850

members.name: resume
members.doc: Ends one pause(); after the outermost one, automatic collections resume at the next safepoint. Extra calls do nothing.

examples.code:
import { gc } from "std/gc"

gc.pause()
const items = ["a", "b", "c"].map((s: string) => s.toUpperCase())
gc.resume()   // automatic collections run again
println(items.join(","))   // A,B,C

members.name: stats
members.doc: The current counters.

examples.code:
import { gc } from "std/gc"

const before = gc.stats().allocatedBytes
const xs = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
const after = gc.stats().allocatedBytes
println(after - before)   // e.g. 64 (0 in the interpreter)

members.name: resetStats
members.doc: Restarts the pause statistics (lastPause, maxPause, totalPause), e.g. after loading, to measure a frame loop.

examples.code:
import { gc } from "std/gc"

gc.collect()
gc.resetStats()
println(gc.stats().maxPause)   // 0

members.name: dumpRoots
members.doc: Debugging: prints the GC roots that hold references to standard output (named locals per active function, innermost first, then globals).

examples.code:
import { gc } from "std/gc"

const names = ["ada", "grace"]
gc.dumpRoots()   // prints the roots, e.g. `names` (nothing in the interpreter)
println(names.length)   // 2

modules.name: std/http
modules.about: std/http: an HTTP/1.1 server (spec §13.2, Deno.serve-shaped). Each request is read whole, handed to the handler as a Request, and its Response written back (Content-Length, or chunked for a stream body); connections are kept alive between requests unless either side says Connection: close.

items.name: ServeOptions
items.doc: Where to listen: port (0 picks a free one) and hostname ("127.0.0.1" by default; "0.0.0.0" for every interface). With cert (a PEM certificate chain) and key (its PEM private key), as in Deno, the server speaks HTTPS.

examples.code:
import { serve } from "std/http"

const server = await serve({ hostname: "127.0.0.1", port: 0 },
  async (req) => new Response("hi"))
println(server.addr.hostname)   // 127.0.0.1
println(server.addr.port > 0)   // true (a free port was picked)
await server.shutdown()

members.name: port
members.doc: The port (8000 by default; 0 picks a free one, which HttpServer.addr tells).

members.name: hostname
members.doc: The address to listen on ("127.0.0.1" by default; "0.0.0.0" for every interface).

members.name: cert
members.doc: The PEM certificate chain for HTTPS (needs key too, or serve throws a NetError).

members.name: key
members.doc: The PEM private key for cert.

items.name: HttpServer
items.doc: A running server: its address, shutdown(), and finished (settles once it has stopped).

members.name: addr
members.doc: The address it listens on (with the actual port when 0 was asked for).

members.name: constructor
members.signature: constructor(listener: Listener, handler: (req: Request) => Promise<Response, Error>)
members.doc: A server for listener's connections; serve makes these (and starts accepting).

members.name: finished
members.doc: Settles once the server has stopped and every connection is closed.

examples.code:
import { serve } from "std/http"

const server = await serve({ port: 0 }, async (req) => new Response("bye"))
server.shutdown()
await server.finished
println("stopped")   // stopped

members.name: shutdown
members.doc: Stops accepting connections, closes idle ones, and lets requests in progress finish.

items.name: serve
items.signature: async function serve(options: ServeOptions, handler: (req: Request) => Promise<Response, Error>): Promise<HttpServer> throws NetError
items.doc: Serves HTTP on options.port, calling handler for each request (a handler that throws gets a 500 response). Resolves once it's listening.

items.name: WebSocketUpgrade
items.doc: What upgradeWebSocket gives: the server's end of the socket, and the response to return from the handler.

members.name: socket
members.doc: The server's end of the connection, usable once response has been sent.

members.name: response
members.doc: The 101 Switching Protocols response to return from the handler.

items.name: upgradeWebSocket
items.signature: function upgradeWebSocket( req: Request, protocol: string = "", options: WebSocketOptions = {}, ): WebSocketUpgrade throws TypeError
items.doc: Accepts a WebSocket request (upgrade: websocket): return response from the handler and use socket (its onopen runs once the response is sent). Anything else throws a TypeError. options.maxMessageBytes limits the messages the socket receives (#67).

modules.name: std/js
modules.about: std/js (spec §12.3): JavaScript values in wasm32-browser programs. A JsValue is a handle to a value the JavaScript glue keeps for pico code (__io 150–168; decision 259); it's released once the JsValue is collected. Every JavaScript operation can throw JsError. js: imports (import { document } from "js:dom") are typed wrappers over these.

items.name: JsError
items.doc: An exception thrown by JavaScript code (its String(e) is the message), or a JavaScript value of the wrong type.

members.name: constructor
members.doc: A JsError with message.

items.name: JsArg
items.signature: type JsArg = f64 | string | bool | JsValue
items.doc: What JavaScript functions take: numbers, strings, booleans and other JavaScript values.

items.name: JsValue
items.doc: A JavaScript value held by pico code.

members.name: handle
members.doc: The runtime's handle of the JavaScript value (0 undefined, 1 null, 2 globalThis).

members.name: constructor
members.doc: Wraps a handle the runtime returned (released when the JsValue is collected); use JsValue.from, jsNull() and jsUndefined() instead.

members.name: from
members.doc: x as a JavaScript value (a number, a string, a boolean, or x itself).

examples.code:
import { JsValue } from "std/js"

// Browser builds only (`--target wasm32-browser`); `pico run` can't run it.
println(JsValue.from(1.5).typeOf())    // number
println(JsValue.from("hi").typeOf())   // string
println(JsValue.from(true).asBool())   // true

members.name: fn
members.signature: public static fn(f: (args: JsValue) => void throws JsError): JsValue
members.doc: A JavaScript function that calls f with its arguments (an array). A JsError f throws is reported on the console (console.error).

members.name: get
members.signature: public get(name: string): JsValue throws JsError

members.name: set
members.signature: public set(name: string, v: JsArg): void throws JsError

members.name: call

members.doc: this[name](...args).

members.name: invoke
members.signature: public invoke(...args: JsArg[]): JsValue throws JsError
members.doc: this(...args) (with undefined as this).

members.name: construct
members.signature: public construct(...args: JsArg[]): JsValue throws JsError
members.doc: new this(...args).

members.name: at
members.signature: public at(i: int): JsValue throws JsError
members.doc: this[i] (arrays, array-likes).

import { js, jsNull } from "std/js"

// Browser builds only (`--target wasm32-browser`); `pico run` can't run it.
println(js.global.get("Math").typeOf())                  // object
println(js.global.get("Math").get("max").typeOf())       // function

items.name: JsObject
items.doc: The base of classes generated from .d.ts files (js: imports): a typed view of a JavaScript object.

members.name: jsValue
members.doc: The JavaScript object this is a view of.

items.name: js

modules.name: std/math
modules.about: std/math (spec §13.2): vectors and matrices for graphics and games (Vec2, Vec3, Vec4, Quat, Mat4: number structs with operators, OpenGL conventions: right-handed, column-major, column vectors), arbitrary-precision integers (BigInt), a seedable random generator (Random) and small helpers. The Math global has the scalar functions. Vectors and quaternions are Formattable: ${v} is (1, 2, 3), ${v:.2f} formats each component.

items.name: clamp
items.signature: function clamp(x: number, lo: number, hi: number): number
items.doc: x limited to lo..hi.

examples.code:
import { clamp } from "std/math"

println(clamp(12, 0, 10))    // 10
println(clamp(-3, 0, 10))    // 0
println(clamp(4.5, 0, 10))   // 4.5

items.doc: The value t of the way from a to b (t = 0 is a, 1 is b).

examples.code:
import { lerp } from "std/math"

println(lerp(10, 20, 0.25))   // 12.5
println(lerp(10, 20, 1))      // 20

import { degToRad } from "std/math"

println(degToRad(180))           // 3.141592653589793

items.name: Vec2

members.name: x
members.doc: The x component.

members.name: y

members.doc: The vector (x, y).

examples.code:
import { Vec2 } from "std/math"

const v = Vec2.of(1.5, 2)
println(`${v}`)   // (1.5, 2)
println(v.x)      // 1.5

println(`${Vec2.zero}`)                   // (0, 0)

members.name: dot
members.doc: The dot product with o.

examples.code:
import { Vec2 } from "std/math"

println(Vec2.of(1, 2).dot(Vec2.of(3, 4)))   // 11
println(Vec2.of(1, 0).dot(Vec2.of(0, 1)))   // 0

members.name: cross
members.doc: The z of the 3D cross product (positive when o is counter-clockwise from this).

examples.code:
import { Vec2 } from "std/math"

println(Vec2.of(1, 0).cross(Vec2.of(0, 1)))   // 1
println(Vec2.of(0, 1).cross(Vec2.of(1, 0)))   // -1

members.name: lengthSquared
members.doc: The squared length (cheaper than length(), for comparisons).

examples.code:
import { Vec2 } from "std/math"

const a = Vec2.of(3, 4)

println(a.lengthSquared() < Vec2.of(6, 0).lengthSquared())   // true

examples.code:

examples.code:

println(`${Vec2.of(0, 5).normalize()}`)   // (0, 1)

members.doc: The Euclidean distance to o.

examples.code:

println(Vec2.of(1, 1).distance(Vec2.of(4, 5)))   // 5

members.name: lerp
members.doc: The point t of the way from this to o (t isn't clamped: outside 0..1 it extrapolates).

members.name: rotate
members.doc: Rotated counter-clockwise by angle radians.

examples.code:
import { Vec2 } from "std/math"

const v = Vec2.of(1, 0).rotate(Math.PI / 2)

println(Vec2.of(1, 0).angle())             // 0

examples.code:

const v = Vec2.of(1.5, 2)
println(`${v:.2f}`)          // (1.50, 2.00)

items.name: Quat
items.doc: A rotation as a unit quaternion w + xi + yj + zk.

members.name: x
members.doc: The x of the vector part (i).

members.name: y
members.doc: The y of the vector part (j).

members.name: z
members.doc: The z of the vector part (k).

members.name: w
members.doc: The scalar part (cos(angle / 2) for a rotation).

members.name: identity
members.doc: No rotation: (0, 0, 0, 1).

examples.code:
import { Quat, Vec3 } from "std/math"

println(`${Quat.identity}`)                       // (0, 0, 0, 1)
println(`${Quat.identity.rotate(Vec3.of(1, 2, 3))}`)   // (1, 2, 3)

members.name: of
members.signature: static of(x: number, y: number, z: number, w: number): Quat
members.doc: The quaternion w + xi + yj + zk, as given (not normalized).

examples.code:
import { Quat } from "std/math"

const q = Quat.of(0, 0, 3, 4)
println(q.length())            // 5
println(`${q.normalize()}`)    // (0, 0, 0.6, 0.8)

members.name: fromAxisAngle
members.signature: static fromAxisAngle(axis: Vec3, angle: number): Quat
members.doc: A rotation by angle radians around axis (normalized here).

members.name: fromEuler
members.signature: static fromEuler(rx: number, ry: number, rz: number): Quat
members.doc: Rotations around x, then y, then z (radians), applied in that order.

examples.code:
import { Quat, Vec3 } from "std/math"

const q = Quat.fromEuler(0, 0, Math.PI / 2)   // a quarter turn around z
println(`${q.rotate(Vec3.unitX):.3f}`)        // (0.000, 1.000, 0.000)

members.name: dot
members.doc: The 4D dot product with o (for unit quaternions, the cosine of half the angle between them).

examples.code:
import { Quat, Vec3 } from "std/math"

const a = Quat.fromAxisAngle(Vec3.unitZ, 0.3)
println(`${a.dot(a):.3f}`)                 // 1.000
println(`${a.dot(Quat.identity):.3f}`)     // 0.989

members.name: length
members.doc: The length (1 for a rotation).

examples.code:
import { Quat, Vec3 } from "std/math"

println(Quat.of(1, 1, 1, 1).length())                            // 2
println(`${Quat.fromAxisAngle(Vec3.unitY, 1.2).length():.3f}`)   // 1.000

members.name: normalize
members.doc: This quaternion with length 1 (a zero quaternion gives Quat.identity).

examples.code:
import { Quat } from "std/math"

println(`${Quat.of(0, 2, 0, 0).normalize()}`)   // (0, 1, 0, 0)
println(`${Quat.of(0, 0, 0, 0).normalize()}`)   // (0, 0, 0, 1)

members.name: conjugate
members.doc: The vector part negated: for a unit quaternion, the opposite rotation (cheaper than inverse()).

members.name: inverse
members.doc: The opposite rotation (the conjugate over the squared length).

examples.code:
import { Quat } from "std/math"

const q = Quat.of(0, 0, 0, 2)
println(`${q.inverse()}`)       // (-0, -0, -0, 0.5)
println(`${q * q.inverse()}`)   // (0, 0, 0, 1)

members.name: rotate
members.doc: v rotated.

members.name: slerp
members.doc: Spherical interpolation along the shorter arc.

examples.code:
import { Quat, Vec3 } from "std/math"

const a = Quat.identity
const b = Quat.fromAxisAngle(Vec3.unitZ, Math.PI / 2)
const half = a.slerp(b, 0.5)   // a turn of π/4
println(`${half.rotate(Vec3.unitX):.3f}`)   // (0.707, 0.707, 0.000)

members.name: toMat4
members.doc: The rotation matrix.

members.name: approxEquals
members.doc: Each component within eps of o's (q and -q are the same rotation but aren't approximately equal).

examples.code:
import { Quat, Vec3 } from "std/math"

const q = Quat.fromAxisAngle(Vec3.unitX, Math.PI / 2)
println(q.approxEquals(Quat.fromEuler(Math.PI / 2, 0, 0)))   // true
println(q.approxEquals(-q))                                  // false

members.name: toString
members.doc: (x, y, z, w), e.g. (0, 0, 0, 1) for the identity.

examples.code:
import { Quat } from "std/math"

println(Quat.identity.toString())   // (0, 0, 0, 1)

members.name: format
members.doc: Each component formatted with spec (${q:.2f}); an invalid spec panics.

items.name: Mat4
items.doc: A 4×4 matrix, column-major (m[col * 4 + row], as OpenGL and WebGPU upload it), acting on column vectors: a * b applies b first.

members.name: m
members.doc: The 16 elements, column-major: the element in row, col is m[col * 4 + row].

members.name: identity
members.doc: The identity matrix.

examples.code:
import { Mat4, Vec3 } from "std/math"

println(`${Mat4.identity.transformPoint(Vec3.of(1, 2, 3))}`)   // (1, 2, 3)
println(Mat4.identity.determinant())                           // 1

members.name: fromColumnMajor
members.doc: From 16 numbers in column-major order.

members.name: fromRows
members.doc: From 16 numbers as written on paper (row by row).

examples.code:
import { Mat4 } from "std/math"

const m = Mat4.fromRows([
  1, 0, 0, 5,
  0, 1, 0, 6,
  0, 0, 1, 7,
  0, 0, 0, 1,
])
println(m.get(1, 3))   // 6

members.name: translation

examples.code:
import { Mat4, Vec3 } from "std/math"

const t = Mat4.translation(Vec3.of(1, 2, 3))

examples.code:
import { Mat4, Vec3 } from "std/math"

examples.code:
import { Mat4, Vec3 } from "std/math"

println(`${Mat4.rotationZ(Math.PI / 2).transformPoint(Vec3.unitX):.3f}`)   // (0.000, 1.000, 0.000)

members.name: fromQuat
members.doc: The rotation matrix of q (expected to be a unit quaternion; it isn't normalized here).

members.name: perspective
members.signature: static perspective(fovy: number, aspect: number, near: number, far: number): Mat4
members.doc: A perspective projection (OpenGL clip space, z in -1..1): fovy radians vertically.

members.name: orthographic
members.signature: static orthographic(left: number, right: number, bottom: number, top: number, near: number, far: number): Mat4
members.doc: An orthographic projection (OpenGL clip space).

import { Mat4, Vec3 } from "std/math"

const proj = Mat4.orthographic(0, 800, 0, 600, -1, 1)

members.name: lookAt
members.signature: static lookAt(eye: Vec3, target: Vec3, up: Vec3): Mat4
members.doc: A view matrix: the camera at eye looking at target, up roughly up. Panics when eye is target, or up is along the view direction (there is no side axis then).

const m = Mat4.translation(Vec3.of(7, 8, 9))

members.name: transformDirection

import { Mat4, Vec3 } from "std/math"

const a = Mat4.translation(Vec3.of(5, 6, 7)).toArray()
println(a.length)                                  // 16

items.name: Random
items.doc: A seedable pseudo-random generator (xoshiro128**): the same seed gives the same sequence on every target. Not for cryptography (use crypto).

examples.code:
import { Random } from "std/math"

const rng = new Random(42)          // the same numbers on every run and target
const die = rng.int(1, 7)           // 1 to 6
println(die >= 1 && die <= 6)       // true
const dice = new Random()           // seeded from the system: different every run
println(dice.float() < 1)           // true

members.name: constructor
members.doc: Seeded with seed, or from the system's randomness without one.

members.name: nextU32
members.doc: 32 random bits (0 .. 2**32).

members.name: float
members.doc: A number in [0, 1).

members.name: int
members.signature: public int(lo: int, hi: int): int
members.doc: An integer in lo .. hi (hi excluded), without bias.

members.name: bool
members.doc: true with probability p.

examples.code:
import { Random } from "std/math"

const rng = new Random()
println(rng.bool(1))   // true
println(rng.bool(0))   // false
println(rng.bool())    // true or false, each half of the time

members.name: pick
members.doc: A random element (panics on an empty array).

members.name: shuffle
members.doc: Shuffles xs in place (Fisher–Yates).

examples.code:
import { Random } from "std/math"

const cards = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
new Random().shuffle(cards)
println(cards.join(" "))   // e.g. 3 1 5 2 4

items.name: BigInt
items.doc: An arbitrary-precision integer: + - * / % (division truncates towards zero, as in JavaScript), comparisons, pow, toString()/toStringRadix(radix) and parse.

examples.code:
import { BigInt } from "std/math"

const a = BigInt.of(2).pow(64)
const b = new BigInt(1000)
println(a)                       // 18446744073709551616
println(a * b + BigInt.of(1))    // 18446744073709551616001
println(a / b)                   // 18446744073709551
println(a % b)                   // 616

members.name: constructor
members.doc: The integer value (every int, i64's minimum included).

examples.code:
import { BigInt } from "std/math"

println(new BigInt(-42))   // -42
println(new BigInt())      // 0

members.name: of
members.doc: The integer value: BigInt.of(n) is new BigInt(n).

examples.code:
import { BigInt } from "std/math"

println(BigInt.of(9007199254740993) * BigInt.of(3))   // 27021597764222979

members.name: parse
members.signature: public static parse(s: string, radix: int = 10): BigInt throws SyntaxError
members.doc: Parses an optionally signed integer in radix (2–36; 0x/0o/0b prefixes with the default radix 10). Throws SyntaxError, as JavaScript's BigInt("…") does.

members.name: isZero
members.doc: Whether the value is 0.

examples.code:
import { BigInt } from "std/math"

println(BigInt.of(0).isZero)                    // true
println((BigInt.of(5) - BigInt.of(5)).isZero)   // true

members.name: isNegative
members.doc: Whether the value is below 0.

examples.code:
import { BigInt } from "std/math"

println(BigInt.of(-3).isNegative)   // true
println(BigInt.of(0).isNegative)    // false

members.name: toInt
members.doc: The value as an int (panics if it doesn't fit).

members.name: toNumber
members.doc: The nearest number.

examples.code:
import { BigInt } from "std/math"

println(BigInt.of(2).pow(70).toNumber())   // 1.1805916207174113e+21

members.name: not
members.doc: Bitwise NOT: -this - 1 (JavaScript's ~ on bigints, #60).

examples.code:
import { BigInt } from "std/math"

println(BigInt.of(5).not())    // -6
println(BigInt.of(-1).not())   // 0

members.name: shiftLeft
members.doc: this * 2 ** n (JavaScript's << on bigints; a negative n shifts right, #60).

examples.code:
import { BigInt } from "std/math"

println(BigInt.of(1).shiftLeft(100))   // 1267650600228229401496703205376
println(BigInt.of(-3).shiftLeft(2))    // -12

members.name: shiftRight
members.doc: this / 2 ** n rounded down, towards negative infinity (JavaScript's >> on bigints; a negative n shifts left, #60).

examples.code:
import { BigInt } from "std/math"

println(BigInt.of(1000).shiftRight(3))   // 125
println(BigInt.of(-9).shiftRight(1))     // -5

members.name: pow
members.doc: this ** e (e >= 0).

examples.code:
import { BigInt } from "std/math"

println(BigInt.of(2).pow(100))   // 1267650600228229401496703205376
println(BigInt.of(7).pow(0))     // 1

members.name: abs
members.doc: The absolute value.

examples.code:
import { BigInt } from "std/math"

println(BigInt.of(-12).abs())   // 12

members.name: compareTo
members.doc: -1, 0 or 1 as this is less than, equal to or greater than o.

members.name: equals
members.doc: Whether this and o are the same integer.

examples.code:
import { BigInt } from "std/math"

println(BigInt.of(2).pow(10).equals(BigInt.of(1024)))   // true

members.name: toString
members.doc: In decimal (also the string form: ${big}).

examples.code:
import { BigInt } from "std/math"

const n = BigInt.of(-2).pow(65)
println(n.toString())   // -36893488147419103232
println(`n = ${n}`)     // n = -36893488147419103232

members.name: format
members.doc: The integer as a template's format spec says (#57), as ints are: d (decimal, the default), x/X (hex), o, b, with +/space signs, # prefixes (0x, 0o, 0b), width, alignment, fill and 0 padding. A precision or a float kind panics.

members.name: toStringRadix
members.doc: In base radix (2–36), lower-case digits (JavaScript's toString(radix)).

examples.code:
import { BigInt } from "std/math"

println(BigInt.of(255).toStringRadix(16))   // ff
println(BigInt.of(-5).toStringRadix(2))     // -101

modules.name: std/meta
modules.about:
std/meta: what decorators see of the declarations they decorate (spec §11.2).

A decorator function takes a ClassDecl (classes and structs) or a FunctionDecl first, then the decorator's own arguments (@route("GET", "/users")). The compiler runs it at compile time, before the decorated declaration is compiled, and applies what it asked for: added members, hidden statics, wrapped bodies and diagnostics. Code is written as strings (template literals), parsed and type-checked where it's spliced in.

items.name: ClassDecl
items.doc: A decorated class or struct.

members.name: id
members.doc: Which declaration this is (for the compiler).

members.name: name
members.doc: The type's name, without type parameters.

members.name: kind
members.doc: "class" or "struct".

members.name: fieldNames
members.doc: The instance fields' names, in declaration order (parameter properties included).

members.name: fieldTypes
members.doc: The instance fields' types as written ("" where a field has no annotation).

members.name: methodNames
members.doc: The instance methods' names (not getters, setters or static methods).

members.name: typeParams
members.doc: The type parameters' names (["T"] for Box<T>).

members.name: constructor
members.signature: constructor( /// Which declaration this is (for the compiler). public id: int, /// The type's name, without type parameters. public name: string, /// `"class"` or `"struct"`. public kind: string, /// The instance fields' names, in declaration order (parameter properties included). public fieldNames: string[], /// The instance fields' types as written (`""` where a field has no annotation). public fieldTypes: string[], /// The instance methods' names (not getters, setters or static methods). public methodNames: string[], /// The type parameters' names (`["T"]` for `Box<T>`). public typeParams: string[], )
members.doc: Made by the compiler for each use of a decorator; a decorator receives it.

members.name: selfType
members.doc: The type as written inside its own declaration: Box<T>.

members.name: fields
members.doc: The instance fields, in declaration order: each one's name and type as written.

members.name: hasField
members.doc: Whether the type declares an instance field called name.

members.name: hasMethod
members.doc: Whether the type declares an instance method called name (before any the decorators add).

members.name: addMember
members.doc: Adds a member written as code: toString(): string { … } or count: int = 0.

members.name: addMethod
members.doc: Adds a method written as code.

members.name: addField
members.doc: Adds a field written as code.

members.name: addStatic
members.signature: public addStatic(name: string, init: string): string
members.doc: Hidden, once-initialized state only generated code can use; returns the name to splice into templates.

members.name: error
members.doc: A compile error at the decorated declaration.

members.name: warn
members.doc: A compile warning at the decorated declaration (the build goes on).

members.name: note
members.doc: A note (information, not a problem) at the decorated declaration.

items.name: FunctionDecl
items.doc: A decorated function.

members.name: id
members.doc: Which declaration this is (for the compiler).

members.name: name
members.doc: The function's name.

members.name: paramNames
members.doc: The parameters' names, in order.

members.name: paramTypes
members.doc: The parameters' types as written ("" where a parameter has no annotation).

members.name: returnType
members.doc: The return type as written ("void" if it isn't).

members.name: isAsync
members.doc: Whether it's an async function.

members.name: constructor
members.signature: constructor( /// Which declaration this is (for the compiler). public id: int, /// The function's name. public name: string, /// The parameters' names, in order. public paramNames: string[], /// The parameters' types as written (`""` where a parameter has no annotation). public paramTypes: string[], /// The return type as written (`"void"` if it isn't). public returnType: string, /// Whether it's an `async function`. public isAsync: bool, )
members.doc: Made by the compiler for each use of a decorator; a decorator receives it.

members.name: params
members.doc: The parameters, in order: each one's name and type as written.

members.name: wrapBody
members.signature: public wrapBody(f: (args: Args, call: string) => string): void
members.doc: Replaces the body with the code f returns: f gets the arguments and the code that calls the original body with them (call).

members.name: addStatic
members.signature: public addStatic(name: string, init: string): string
members.doc: Hidden, once-initialized state only generated code can use; returns the name to splice into templates.

members.name: error
members.doc: A compile error at the decorated declaration.

members.name: warn
members.doc: A compile warning at the decorated declaration (the build goes on).

members.name: note
members.doc: A note (information, not a problem) at the decorated declaration.

items.name: Args
items.doc: The ${}-spliceable arguments of a wrapped function's call.

members.name: names
members.doc: Made by the compiler for wrapBody. names: the parameters' names, in order.

members.name: constructor
members.doc: Made by the compiler for wrapBody. names: the parameters' names, in order.

members.name: list
members.doc: The arguments as an argument list: a, b.

members.name: hashKey
members.doc: Code computing a u64 hash of the arguments (they must be Hashable).

items.name: ast
items.doc: The AST builder: code for generated declarations, built piece by piece (each piece is code text, so it splices into templates too: ${ast.string(fn.name)}).

members.name: string
members.doc: A string literal: ast.string("a\"b") is "a\"b".

examples.code:
import { ast } from "std/meta"

println(ast.string("say \"hi\""))   // "say \"hi\""

members.name: int
members.doc: An integer literal: ast.int(42) is 42.

examples.code:
import { ast } from "std/meta"

println(ast.int(42))   // 42

members.name: bool
members.doc: A boolean literal: true or false.

examples.code:
import { ast } from "std/meta"

println(ast.bool(true))   // true

members.name: ident
members.doc: A name, checked to be an identifier.

examples.code:
import { ast } from "std/meta"

println(ast.ident("count"))   // count

members.name: field
members.doc: this.name

examples.code:
import { ast } from "std/meta"

println(ast.field("name"))   // this.name

members.name: member
members.signature: public static member(object: string, name: string): string
members.doc: object.name

examples.code:
import { ast } from "std/meta"

println(ast.member("user", "email"))   // user.email

members.name: call
members.signature: public static call(callee: string, ...args: string[]): string
members.doc: callee(a, b)

examples.code:
import { ast } from "std/meta"

println(ast.call("max", "a", ast.int(0)))   // max(a, 0)

members.name: binary
members.signature: public static binary(left: string, op: string, right: string): string
members.doc: (left op right)

examples.code:
import { ast } from "std/meta"

println(ast.binary("a", "*", ast.int(2)))   // (a * 2)

members.name: concat
members.doc: a + b + … of strings, as one string expression ("" for none).

examples.code:
import { ast } from "std/meta"

println(ast.concat(ast.string("id="), ast.field("id")))   // ("id=" + this.id)

members.name: returns
members.doc: return value

examples.code:
import { ast } from "std/meta"

println(ast.returns(ast.field("total")))   // return this.total

members.name: constant
members.signature: public static constant(name: string, value: string): string
members.doc: const name = value

examples.code:
import { ast } from "std/meta"

println(ast.constant("limit", ast.int(10)))   // const limit = 10

members.name: block
members.doc: { statements }

members.name: method
members.signature: public static method(name: string, ...statements: string[]): string
members.doc: A public method without parameters: name() { statements }.

members.name: typedMethod
members.signature: public static typedMethod(name: string, params: string[], returns: string, ...statements: string[]): string
members.doc: A public method with parameters ("x: i64", …) and a return type.

modules.name: std/net
modules.about: std/net: TCP (listen, connect), Unix-domain sockets (listenUnix, connectUnix), UDP (bind) and DNS (resolve), spec §13.4. The implementation is in the core library (<core>/net.pi), which fetch uses too.

items.name: TcpStream
items.doc: A TCP (or Unix-domain) connection as a ByteStream (std/streams), for protocol code that takes any byte stream.

members.name: conn
members.doc: The connection.

examples.code:
import { listen, connect, TcpStream } from "std/net"
import { ByteStream } from "std/streams"

const server = await listen(0)
const stream: ByteStream = new TcpStream(await connect(server.addr.port))
println(server.addr.hostname)   // 127.0.0.1
stream.close()
server.close()

members.name: write
members.signature: public async write(bytes: Uint8Array): Promise<void> throws Error

items.name: UdpStream
items.doc: A UDP socket as a ByteStream: datagrams from anyone are read; writes go to peerPort and peerHost, or, until one is given, to whoever sent the last datagram read (and are dropped while nobody has).

members.name: socket
members.doc: The socket.

members.name: constructor
members.signature: constructor(socket: UdpSocket, peerPort: int? = null, peerHost: string? = null)

members.name: read
members.signature: public async read(): Promise<Uint8Array?> throws Error

members.name: write
members.signature: public async write(bytes: Uint8Array): Promise<void> throws Error
members.doc: Sends bytes as one datagram.

items.name: listen
items.signature: function listen(port: int = 0, hostname: string = "127.0.0.1"): Promise<Listener, NetError>
items.doc: Listens for TCP connections on hostname ("0.0.0.0" or "::" for every interface) and port (0 picks a free one; see addr).

examples.code:
import { listen } from "std/net"

const listener = await listen(0, "127.0.0.1")
println(listener.addr.port > 0)   // true
listener.close()

items.name: connect
items.signature: function connect(port: int, hostname: string = "127.0.0.1"): Promise<Conn, NetError>
items.doc: Connects to hostname (a name or an IP address) and port over TCP.

items.name: listenUnix
items.doc: Listens for connections on a Unix-domain socket at path (macOS, Linux and Windows 10 and later; not WASI) (#85). The socket file must not exist yet (AddrInUse); closing the listener removes it. addr is { hostname: path, port: -1 }.

items.name: connectUnix
items.doc: Connects to the Unix-domain socket at path (#85).

items.name: bind
items.signature: function bind(port: int = 0, hostname: string = "127.0.0.1", options: BindOptions? = null): Promise<UdpSocket, NetError>
items.doc: A UDP socket on hostname and port (0 picks a free one; see addr). options: see BindOptions (sharing the port, for multicast).

examples.code:
import { bind } from "std/net"

const socket = await bind(0, "127.0.0.1")
println(socket.addr.port > 0)   // true
socket.close()

items.name: resolve
items.doc: The IP addresses of hostname (in the order the system gives them, without repeats).

examples.code:
import { resolve } from "std/net"

println((await resolve("127.0.0.1")).join(", "))      // 127.0.0.1
const local = await resolve("localhost")
println(local.length > 0)                            // true (e.g. 127.0.0.1 and ::1)

items.name: networkInterfaces
items.doc: The machine's network interfaces, one entry per address (an interface with an IPv4 and an IPv6 address has two). Empty where the platform can't tell (WASI, the browser).

items.name: BindOptions
items.doc: Options of bind (#214).

members.name: reuseAddress
members.doc: Lets other sockets bind the same address and port (SO_REUSEADDR, and SO_REUSEPORT where there is one), so several programs can receive one multicast group's datagrams.

items.name: NetworkInterface
items.doc: One address of a network interface (networkInterfaces).

members.name: name
members.doc: The interface's name (lo, eth0, en0, Ethernet, …).

members.name: address
members.doc: The address, as text.

members.name: up
members.doc: Whether it's up.

members.name: loopback
members.doc: Whether it's the loopback interface.

members.name: multicast
members.doc: Whether it can send and receive multicast.

items.name: NetError
items.doc: A failed network operation: the address it was about (host:port), a message (connection refused: 127.0.0.1:9) and a portable kind ("ConnectionRefused", "ConnectionReset", "AddrInUse", "AddrNotAvailable", "TimedOut", "HostNotFound", "InvalidData", "PermissionDenied", "TlsError" (a failed TLS handshake: the message says why, such as an untrusted certificate), "Other").

members.name: address
members.doc: What the operation was about: usually host:port ([::1]:80 for IPv6), the host name alone for a failed lookup.

members.name: kind
members.doc: The portable kind ("ConnectionRefused", "TimedOut", …; see above).

members.name: constructor
members.signature: constructor(address: string, message: string, kind: string)
members.doc: A NetError about address with message and kind.

examples.code:
const e = new NetError("example.com:443", "timed out: example.com:443", "TimedOut")
println(e.kind)      // TimedOut
println(e.address)   // example.com:443
println(e.message)   // timed out: example.com:443

items.name: Addr
items.doc: An IP address and a port.

examples.code:
import { listen } from "std/net"

const listener = await listen(0, "127.0.0.1")
const addr: Addr = listener.addr
println(addr.hostname)   // 127.0.0.1
println(addr.port > 0)   // true (a free port the system picked)
listener.close()

members.name: hostname
members.doc: The IP address ("127.0.0.1", "::1", without brackets), or a Unix-domain socket's path.

members.name: port
members.doc: The port number; -1 for a Unix-domain socket.

items.name: Conn
items.doc: A TCP connection: chunks of bytes with read or for await, the rest as text with text(), writes (in the order they're made) with write/writeText. One read at a time.

members.name: localAddr
members.doc: This side's address.

members.name: remoteAddr
members.doc: The other side's address.

members.name: constructor
members.signature: constructor(fd: int, localAddr: Addr, remoteAddr: Addr)
members.doc: A connection on descriptor fd; made by connect and accept, not by programs.

members.name: readable
members.doc: The connection's incoming bytes as a stream (reading it and read() don't mix).

members.name: writable
members.doc: The connection's outgoing bytes as a stream: closing it finishes writing (closeWrite()), aborting it closes the connection.

members.name: read
members.doc: Up to n bytes (as soon as some arrive), or null once the other side has finished writing (or this side is closed).

members.name: next
members.doc: for await reads chunks until the end.

members.name: asyncIterator
members.doc: The connection itself (for await (const chunk of conn)).

members.name: text
members.doc: Everything until the other side finishes writing, as text (UTF-8; anything else rejects with kind "InvalidData").

members.name: write
members.doc: Writes all of data; the count written.

members.name: writeText
members.doc: Writes text as UTF-8; the count of bytes written.

members.name: setNoDelay
members.signature: public setNoDelay(noDelay: bool = true): void throws NetError
members.doc: Turns Nagle's algorithm off (noDelay, the default) or on: small writes go out at once instead of waiting to be coalesced (TCP_NODELAY, #65). Throws a NetError where the system can't (WASI).

members.name: setKeepAlive
members.signature: public setKeepAlive(enable: bool = false, initialDelay: int = 0): void throws NetError
members.doc: Turns TCP keep-alive probes on (enable) or off (#65); initialDelay is how long the connection idles before the first probe, in milliseconds (0: the system's default; rounded up to seconds). Throws a NetError where the system can't (WASI).

members.name: closeWrite
members.doc: Finishes writing once earlier writes are done (the other side reads the end); reading goes on.

members.name: close
members.doc: Closes the connection once earlier writes are done: a waiting read ends with null. Twice is fine.

items.name: Listener
items.doc: A TCP listener: accept() or for await (const conn of listener).

members.name: addr
members.doc: The address it listens on (with the port chosen when listen was given 0).

members.name: constructor
members.doc: A listener on descriptor fd; made by listen, not by programs.

members.name: accept
members.doc: The next connection, or null once the listener is closed. Several calls at once each get a connection (#65: a call made while another waits accepts after it).

members.name: next
members.doc: for await accepts connections until the listener is closed.

members.name: asyncIterator
members.doc: The listener itself (for await (const conn of listener)).

members.name: close
members.doc: Stops listening: a waiting accept() gives null (twice is fine). Open connections stay open.

items.name: Datagram
items.doc: A received datagram and where it came from.

members.name: data
members.doc: The datagram's bytes (cut to the size receive asked for).

members.name: addr
members.doc: The address it came from.

items.name: UdpSocket
items.doc: A UDP socket: send datagrams anywhere, receive them one at a time.

members.name: addr
members.doc: The address it's bound to (with the port chosen when bind was given 0).

members.name: constructor
members.doc: A socket on descriptor fd; made by bind, not by programs.

members.name: addMembership
members.signature: public addMembership(group: string, interfaceAddress: string = ""): void throws NetError
members.doc: Joins multicast group group (an IPv4 or IPv6 address): datagrams sent to it arrive here too. interfaceAddress picks the interface (its IPv4 address, or for IPv6 its name); "" lets the system choose. Bind to "0.0.0.0" (or "::") and the group's port.

examples.code:
import { bind } from "std/net"

const socket = await bind(0, "0.0.0.0", { reuseAddress: true })
socket.addMembership("239.255.0.1")
socket.dropMembership("239.255.0.1")
socket.close()

members.name: dropMembership
members.signature: public dropMembership(group: string, interfaceAddress: string = ""): void throws NetError
members.doc: Leaves multicast group group (joined with addMembership).

examples.code:
import { bind } from "std/net"

const socket = await bind(0, "0.0.0.0")
socket.addMembership("239.255.0.1")
socket.dropMembership("239.255.0.1")
socket.close()

members.name: setMulticastTTL
members.signature: public setMulticastTTL(ttl: int): void throws NetError
members.doc: How many hops the multicast datagrams it sends may take (1 by default: this network only; mDNS uses 255).

examples.code:
import { bind } from "std/net"

const socket = await bind(0, "0.0.0.0")
socket.setMulticastTTL(255)
socket.close()

members.name: setMulticastLoopback
members.signature: public setMulticastLoopback(on: bool): void throws NetError
members.doc: Whether the multicast datagrams it sends come back to this machine's sockets too (on by default).

examples.code:
import { bind } from "std/net"

const socket = await bind(0, "0.0.0.0")
socket.setMulticastLoopback(false)
socket.close()

members.name: setMulticastInterface
members.signature: public setMulticastInterface(interfaceAddress: string): void throws NetError
members.doc: The interface its multicast datagrams go out on: its IPv4 address (for an IPv6 socket, its name). See networkInterfaces.

examples.code:
import { bind } from "std/net"

const socket = await bind(0, "0.0.0.0")
socket.setMulticastInterface("127.0.0.1")
socket.close()

members.name: send
members.signature: public send(data: Uint8Array, port: int, hostname: string = "127.0.0.1"): Promise<int, NetError>
members.doc: Sends data as one datagram to hostname and port; the count of bytes sent.

members.name: sendText
members.signature: public sendText(text: string, port: int, hostname: string = "127.0.0.1"): Promise<int, NetError>
members.doc: Sends text (as UTF-8) as one datagram.

members.name: receive
members.doc: The next datagram (at most n bytes of it; the rest is dropped), or null once the socket is closed. One at a time.

members.name: close
members.doc: Closes the socket: a waiting receive() gives null (twice is fine).

modules.name: std/os
modules.about:
std/os (spec §13.4): where things go on this system: the home directory, the temporary directory, and the per-user directories for an application's data, caches and configuration.

           Linux (XDG)                       macOS                           Windows

data $XDG_DATA_HOME, ~/.local/share ~/Library/Application Support %APPDATA% localData as data as data %LOCALAPPDATA% cache $XDG_CACHE_HOME, ~/.cache ~/Library/Caches %LOCALAPPDATA% config $XDG_CONFIG_HOME, ~/.config ~/Library/Application Support %APPDATA% state $XDG_STATE_HOME, ~/.local/state — —

They come from the environment (a variable that is empty or not an absolute path is ignored, as the XDG specification says), so they can be null when nothing says. Nothing is created: an application makes its own directory below one of them.

items.name: platform
items.doc: This build's system: "linux", "macos", "windows" or "wasi".

items.name: UserDirs
items.doc: The per-user directories (see userDirs); null where nothing says.

examples.code:
import { userDirs } from "std/os"

const vars = new Map<string, string>()
vars.set("HOME", "/home/ada")
const dirs = userDirs(vars, "linux")
println(dirs.home)     // /home/ada
println(dirs.cache)    // /home/ada/.cache
println(dirs.config)   // /home/ada/.config

items.name: userDirs
items.signature: function userDirs(vars: Map<string, string>, os: string = platform): UserDirs
items.doc: The directories for the environment vars on system os (platform's values): what the other functions give, for this process. For tests, and for code that works out another system's.

examples.code:
import { userDirs } from "std/os"

const vars = new Map<string, string>()
vars.set("HOME", "/home/ada")
vars.set("XDG_CONFIG_HOME", "/etc/ada")
println(userDirs(vars, "linux").config)   // /etc/ada
println(userDirs(vars, "linux").state)    // /home/ada/.local/state
println(userDirs(vars, "macos").cache)    // /home/ada/Library/Caches
println(userDirs(vars, "windows").home)   // null

items.name: homeDir
items.doc: The user's home directory: $HOME (%USERPROFILE% on Windows).

examples.code:
import { homeDir } from "std/os"

println(homeDir())   // e.g. /home/ada

items.name: dataDir
items.doc: For data that must survive: settings, user files (roaming on Windows).

items.name: localDataDir
items.doc: For data that stays on this machine (Windows' %LOCALAPPDATA%; elsewhere dataDir()).

examples.code:
import { localDataDir } from "std/os"

println(localDataDir())   // e.g. /home/ada/.local/share

items.name: cacheDir
items.doc: For what can be rebuilt: downloads, indexes. The user or the system may delete it.

items.name: configDir
items.doc: For configuration files.

examples.code:
import { configDir } from "std/os"
import { join } from "std/path"

const dir = configDir() ?? "."
println(join(dir, "myapp", "settings.json"))   // e.g. /home/ada/.config/myapp/settings.json

items.name: stateDir
items.doc: For state worth keeping between runs but not worth backing up: logs, history (Linux only).

examples.code:
import { stateDir } from "std/os"

println(stateDir())   // e.g. /home/ada/.local/state (null on macOS and Windows)

items.name: tmpDir
items.doc: The directory for temporary files: $TMPDIR (%TEMP%, %TMP% on Windows), else /tmp (C:\Windows\Temp).

examples.code:
import { tmpDir } from "std/os"
import { join } from "std/path"

println(tmpDir())                       // e.g. /tmp
println(join(tmpDir(), "scratch.txt"))  // e.g. /tmp/scratch.txt

modules.name: std/path
modules.about: std/path: file paths (spec §13.4), as Node's path: posix and win32 have both flavours on every platform, and the module's own functions are the platform's (win32 on Windows, posix elsewhere; decision 250). The Windows functions follow Node's path.win32: \ and / both separate, drive letters (C:) and UNC roots (\\server\share), results use \; comparisons in relative ignore case. Not yet: the per-drive working directories (resolve("D:x") uses D:\), \\?\ paths, toNamespacedPath.

items.name: posix
items.doc: POSIX paths (/ separates, : delimits PATH lists) on any platform: posix.join("a", "b") is a/b.

items.name: win32
items.doc: Windows paths (\ separates, / is accepted too, ; delimits PATH lists; drive letters and UNC prefixes) on any platform.

items.name: sep
items.doc: The separator between path segments (\ on Windows).

items.name: delimiter
items.doc: The separator between paths in lists such as PATH (; on Windows).

items.name: isAbsolute
items.doc: Whether p starts at a root (/; on Windows also C:\ and \\server\share).

examples.code:
import { isAbsolute } from "std/path"

println(isAbsolute("/usr/bin"))      // true
println(isAbsolute("src/main.pi"))   // false

items.name: normalize
items.doc: p without . segments, .. segments that follow a name, and repeated separators (a//b/../c/ → a/c/); "" → ".".

examples.code:
import { normalize } from "std/path"

println(normalize("a//b/../c/"))   // a/c/
println(normalize("./x/./y"))      // x/y
println(normalize(""))             // .

items.name: join
items.doc: The parts joined with the separator, normalized (join("a", "../b", "c") → b/c).

examples.code:
import { join } from "std/path"

println(join("src", "lib", "main.pi"))   // src/lib/main.pi
println(join("a", "../b", "c"))          // b/c

items.name: resolve
items.doc: An absolute path: the parts from the last absolute one (or the working directory), joined and normalized, without a trailing separator.

examples.code:
import { resolve } from "std/path"
import { cwd } from "std/process"

println(resolve("/srv", "app", "../data"))              // /srv/data
println(resolve("notes.txt") == cwd() + "/notes.txt")   // true

items.name: dirname
items.doc: The directory part (/a/b/c → /a/b, a → ., /a → /).

examples.code:
import { dirname } from "std/path"

println(dirname("/a/b/c"))   // /a/b
println(dirname("/a"))       // /
println(dirname("a"))        // .

items.name: basename
items.signature: function basename(p: string, ext: string = ""): string
items.doc: The last segment (/a/b.txt → b.txt), without ext if it ends with it.

examples.code:
import { basename } from "std/path"

println(basename("/a/b.txt"))           // b.txt
println(basename("/a/b.txt", ".txt"))   // b

items.name: extname
items.doc: The extension of the last segment, from its last . (a.tar.gz → .gz; .bashrc → "").

examples.code:
import { extname } from "std/path"

println(extname("photo.jpg"))   // .jpg
println(extname("a.tar.gz"))    // .gz
println(extname(".bashrc") == "")   // true

items.name: relative
items.signature: function relative(from: string, to: string): string
items.doc: The path from from to to (both resolved first; "" if they're the same).

examples.code:
import { relative } from "std/path"

println(relative("/srv/app/src", "/srv/app/docs/a.md"))   // ../docs/a.md
println(relative("/srv/app", "/srv/app/src/main.pi"))     // src/main.pi

modules.name: std/posix
modules.about:
std/posix (spec §12.3; Linux and macOS): the POSIX calls packages that talk to devices need, declared once. C header imports leave out variadic functions (open, fcntl, ioctl) and macros that glibc builds from others (O_CLOEXEC), so packages used to declare their own; two declarations of one C symbol with different signatures don't link, so they must come from here. The others have c:unistd.h's parameters (a buffer is ptr<u8>, which is void * to the linker), so a program can use both. Buffers go to C as ptr.bytes(view) inside unsafe.

import { open, close, ioctl, errno, errnoMessage, O_RDWR, O_CLOEXEC } from "std/posix"
const fd = open("/dev/ttyUSB0", (O_RDWR | O_CLOEXEC) as c_int)
if (fd < 0) throw new Error(errnoMessage())

items.name: errno
items.doc: errno: why the last failed call failed (read it right after the call).

examples.code:
import { open, errno, O_RDONLY, ENOENT } from "std/posix"

const fd = open("/no/such/file", O_RDONLY as c_int)
println(fd)                 // -1
println(errno() == ENOENT)  // true

items.name: errnoMessage
items.doc: The system's text for error number e (strerror), by default the last one.

modules.name: std/process
modules.about: std/process: this process (args, argv0, execPath, env, exit, cwd, pid, stdin/stdout/stderr) and external processes (Command), spec §13.2 and §13.3. Programs run without a shell (arguments are passed as an array) unless Command.shell asks for one. Reading or writing a pipe and waiting for a child are jobs on runtime threads that settle on the event loop.

items.name: ProcessError
items.doc: A process that couldn't be started (or whose output couldn't be read as text): the program, a message and a portable kind (as IoError's: "NotFound", "PermissionDenied", "InvalidData", "Other", …).

members.name: command
members.doc: The program that was to run.

members.name: kind
members.doc: The portable kind, as IoError's ("NotFound", "PermissionDenied", "InvalidData", "Other", …).

members.name: constructor
members.signature: constructor(command: string, message: string, kind: string)
members.doc: An error for command with message and kind.

items.name: args
items.doc: The program's arguments (without the program itself).

items.name: argv0
items.doc: The program as it was started: the first word of its command line as given (./pm, pm, C:\bin\pm.exe), which names it (commander's nameFromFilename); under pico run --interp, the entry file. "" when there's none.

items.name: execPath
items.doc: The running program's file as an absolute path, symlinks resolved (an executable found through PATH or a link too): what's next to it is the program's. Under pico run --interp, the entry file. null where it can't be known (WASI).

items.name: pid
items.doc: The process id.

items.name: cwd
items.doc: The working directory.

examples.code:
import { cwd } from "std/process"
import { join } from "std/path"

println(cwd())                         // e.g. /home/ada/project
println(join(cwd(), "project.json"))   // e.g. /home/ada/project/project.json

items.name: exit
items.doc: Ends the process at once with exit code code (no finally blocks run, and pending promises are dropped).

items.name: Env
items.doc: The environment variables (env.get("HOME")). Changes are seen by commands started later.

examples.code:
import { env } from "std/process"

println(env.get("HOME"))   // e.g. /home/ada
env.set("GREETING", "hi")
println(env.get("GREETING"))   // hi

members.name: get
members.doc: The variable's value, or null when it isn't set.

examples.code:
import { env } from "std/process"

const editor = env.get("EDITOR") ?? "vi"
println(editor)                         // e.g. vim
println(env.get("SURELY_NOT_SET_XYZ"))  // null

members.name: has
members.doc: Whether the variable is set (to anything, "" too).

examples.code:
import { env } from "std/process"

env.set("EMPTY", "")
println(env.has("EMPTY"))               // true
println(env.has("SURELY_NOT_SET_XYZ"))  // false

members.name: set
members.signature: public set(name: string, value: string): void
members.doc: Sets the variable to value for this process and the commands it starts later.

examples.code:
import { env, Command } from "std/process"

env.set("APP_MODE", "test")
const out = await Command.shell("echo $APP_MODE").output()
println(out.stdout.trim())   // test

members.name: delete
members.doc: Unsets the variable (nothing happens if it isn't set).

examples.code:
import { env } from "std/process"

env.set("TEMP_FLAG", "1")
env.delete("TEMP_FLAG")
println(env.has("TEMP_FLAG"))   // false

members.name: toObject
members.doc: Every variable, by name.

examples.code:
import { env } from "std/process"

const vars = env.toObject()
println(vars.has("PATH"))   // true
println(vars.size > 0)      // true

items.name: env
items.doc: This process's environment variables.

items.name: Reader
items.doc: The reading end of a pipe (a child's stdout/stderr) or this process's stdin: chunks of bytes with read, for await, or everything at once with text(). One read at a time.

examples.code:
import { Command } from "std/process"

const child = new Command("echo", ["hello"], stdout: "pipe").spawn()
println((await child.stdout.text()).trim())   // hello
await child.status()

members.name: name
members.doc: The stream's name ("stdin", "stdout" or "stderr"), used in panics and as the path of its IoErrors.

members.name: constructor
members.signature: constructor(fd: int, name: string, piped: bool)
members.doc: A reader of descriptor fd (reading panics unless piped); Command and stdin make these.

examples.code:
import { Reader, stdin } from "std/process"

const input: Reader = stdin   // `stdin` and a piped child's `stdout`/`stderr` are Readers
println(input.name)           // stdin

members.name: isTerminal
members.doc: Whether it reads from a terminal (#158): stdin.isTerminal is false when input is piped.

members.name: readable
members.doc: The bytes as a stream (reading it and read() don't mix).

members.name: read
members.doc: Up to n bytes (as soon as some are there), or null at the end.

members.name: close
members.doc: Stops reading (#100): a pending read() settles with null, as at the end, and so do later ones. The descriptor is closed once nothing reads it (this process's stdin stays open). Use it for a pipe or device whose other end may never write or close (a child that keeps running, a serial port, a pty).

examples.code:
import { Command } from "std/process"

const child = new Command("sleep", ["5"], stdout: "pipe").spawn()
const pending = child.stdout.read()
child.stdout.close()
println(await pending)   // null
child.kill()
await child.status()

members.name: next
members.doc: for await reads chunks of bytes until the end.

members.name: asyncIterator
members.doc: for await uses the reader itself.

members.name: text
members.doc: The rest of the stream as text (UTF-8; anything else rejects with kind "InvalidData").

items.name: Writer
items.doc: The writing end of a pipe (a child's stdin) or this process's stdout/stderr. Writes happen in the order they're made; close() (after them) ends the child's input.

examples.code:
import { Command } from "std/process"

const child = new Command("cat", stdin: "pipe", stdout: "pipe").spawn()
await child.stdin.writeText("piped through cat")
child.stdin.close()
println(await child.stdout.text())   // piped through cat
await child.status()

members.name: name
members.doc: The stream's name ("stdin", "stdout" or "stderr"), used in panics and as the path of its IoErrors.

members.name: constructor
members.signature: constructor(fd: int, name: string, piped: bool)
members.doc: A writer to descriptor fd (writing panics unless piped); Command, stdout and stderr make these.

examples.code:
import { Writer, stdout } from "std/process"

const out: Writer = stdout   // `stdout`, `stderr` and a piped child's `stdin` are Writers
println(out.name)            // stdout

members.name: writable
members.doc: The writer as a stream: closing it closes the pipe.

examples.code:
import { Command } from "std/process"

const child = new Command("cat", stdin: "pipe", stdout: "pipe").spawn()
const writer = child.stdin.writable.getWriter()
await writer.write(new TextEncoder().encode("via a stream"))
await writer.close()
println(await child.stdout.text())   // via a stream
await child.status()

members.name: write
members.doc: Writes all of data; the count written.

examples.code:
import { stdout } from "std/process"

const n = await stdout.write(new TextEncoder().encode("bytes\n"))   // bytes
println(n)                                                           // 6

members.name: isTerminal
members.doc: Whether it writes to a terminal (#158): stdout.isTerminal is false when the output is piped or redirected.

members.name: hasColors
members.doc: Whether text written here should have colours (decision 344), as command-line tools commonly decide: no when NO_COLOR is set to anything but "", or FORCE_COLOR is 0 or false; yes when FORCE_COLOR is set to anything else but "", or CLICOLOR_FORCE is set; otherwise whether it writes to a terminal.

examples.code:
import { stdout } from "std/process"

const red = if (stdout.hasColors()) "\u{1b}[31merror\u{1b}[0m" else "error"
println(red)   // error (in red on a colour terminal)

members.name: columns
members.doc: The terminal's width in columns, or null when it isn't one (#158).

examples.code:
import { stdout } from "std/process"

const width = stdout.columns ?? 80
println("-".repeat(width))   // a line as wide as the terminal (80 when it isn't one)

members.name: rows
members.doc: The terminal's height in rows, or null when it isn't one.

examples.code:
import { stdout } from "std/process"

println(stdout.rows ?? 24)   // the terminal's height, e.g. 50 (24 when it isn't one)

members.name: writeText
members.doc: Writes text as UTF-8; the count of bytes written.

examples.code:
import { stdout, stderr } from "std/process"

await stdout.writeText("no newline, ")
await stdout.writeText("then one\n")    // no newline, then one
await stderr.writeText("a warning\n")   // (on standard error) a warning

members.name: close
members.doc: Closes the pipe once earlier writes are done (twice is fine; for stdout/stderr nothing happens).

examples.code:
import { Command } from "std/process"

const child = new Command("wc", ["-c"], stdin: "pipe", stdout: "pipe").spawn()
child.stdin.writeText("12345")
child.stdin.close()   // after the write: wc sees the end of its input
println((await child.stdout.text()).trim())   // 5
await child.status()

items.name: stdin
items.doc: This process's standard input.

items.name: stdout
items.doc: This process's standard output: writes are in order with print.

items.name: stderr
items.doc: This process's standard error: writes are in order with print.

items.name: Stdio
items.doc: What a child's standard stream is connected to: this process's ("inherit"), a pipe to this process ("pipe"), or nothing ("null").

items.name: ExitStatus
items.doc: How a child ended: code is its exit code (128 + the signal's number when a signal ended it, as shells report it).

examples.code:
import { Command, ExitStatus } from "std/process"

const s: ExitStatus = await Command.shell("exit 3").status()
println(s.success)   // false
println(s.code)      // 3
println(s.signal)    // null

members.name: success
members.doc: Whether it exited with code 0 (and no signal ended it).

members.name: code
members.doc: The exit code (128 + the signal's number when a signal ended it).

members.name: signal
members.doc: The number of the signal that ended it (on Windows, the one kill was given), or null.

items.name: Output
items.doc: A finished child's status and everything it wrote (as UTF-8 text).

examples.code:
import { Command, Output } from "std/process"

const out: Output = await new Command("echo", ["hi"]).output()
println(out.success)          // true
println(out.stdout.trim())    // hi
println(out.stderr == "")     // true

members.name: success
members.doc: Whether it exited with code 0 (and no signal ended it).

members.name: code
members.doc: The exit code (128 + the signal's number when a signal ended it).

members.name: signal
members.doc: The number of the signal that ended it (on Windows, the one kill was given), or null.

members.name: stdout
members.doc: Everything it wrote to its standard output ("" when that wasn't piped).

members.name: stderr
members.doc: Everything it wrote to its standard error ("" when that wasn't piped).

items.name: Child
items.doc: A started process: its pipes (where piped), status(), kill().

examples.code:
import { Command } from "std/process"

const child = new Command("echo", ["from a child"], stdout: "pipe").spawn()
println(child.pid > 0)                   // true
println((await child.stdout.text()).trim())   // from a child
println((await child.status()).success)  // true

members.name: pid
members.doc: 0 when it couldn't be started.

members.name: stdin
members.doc: Its standard input, when spawned with stdin: "pipe" (writing to it otherwise panics).

members.name: stdout
members.doc: Its standard output, when spawned with stdout: "pipe" (reading it otherwise panics).

members.name: stderr
members.doc: Its standard error, when spawned with stderr: "pipe" (reading it otherwise panics).

members.name: constructor
members.signature: constructor(pid: int, program: string, error: ProcessError?, stdin: Writer, stdout: Reader, stderr: Reader)
members.doc: A child with process id pid (0 and an error when it couldn't start); Command.spawn makes these.

examples.code:
import { Command, Child } from "std/process"

const child: Child = new Command("true").spawn()   // Command.spawn makes Children
println((await child.status()).code)               // 0

members.name: status
members.doc: Waits for the child to end (rejects when it couldn't be started). Every call gives the same promise.

members.name: output
members.signature: public async output(): Promise<Output> throws ProcessError
members.doc: Everything the child writes to its piped stdout and stderr (as text), and how it ended.

members.name: kill
members.doc: Sends the child a signal (SIGTERM by default; on Windows it's terminated). Nothing happens once it has ended.

items.name: Command
items.doc: A program to run: its arguments (passed as they are, never through a shell), working directory, environment (env adds to or replaces this process's variables; with clearEnv it's all there is) and standard streams. spawn() starts it; output() and status() start it and wait.

members.name: program
members.doc: The program to run: a path, or a name looked up in PATH.

members.name: args
members.doc: The arguments after the program.

members.name: constructor
members.signature: constructor(program: string, args: string[] = [], cwd: string? = null, env: Map<string, string>? = null, clearEnv: bool = false, stdin: Stdio = "inherit", stdout: Stdio = "inherit", stderr: Stdio = "inherit")
members.doc: A command running program with args, in cwd (a relative one is resolved against the working directory; this process's by default), with env added to (or, with clearEnv, instead of) this process's variables, and each standard stream "inherit"ed, "pipe"d or "null". Nothing runs until spawn, output or status.

members.name: shell
members.signature: public static shell(script: string, cwd: string? = null, env: Map<string, string>? = null, clearEnv: bool = false, stdin: Stdio = "inherit", stdout: Stdio = "inherit", stderr: Stdio = "inherit"): Command
members.doc: script run by the platform's shell (/bin/sh -c; cmd.exe /c on Windows).

members.name: spawn
members.doc: Starts the program. If it can't be started, the child's status() rejects with a ProcessError.

examples.code:
import { Command } from "std/process"

const child = new Command("echo", ["spawned"], stdout: "pipe").spawn()
println((await child.stdout.text()).trim())   // spawned
await child.status()

members.name: output
members.doc: Runs the program with its stdout and stderr piped and waits for it: what it wrote and how it ended.

examples.code:
import { Command } from "std/process"

const out = await new Command("ls", ["/"]).output()
println(out.success)                     // true
println(out.stdout.split("\n").length > 1)   // true

members.name: status
members.doc: Runs the program and waits for it to end.

modules.name: std/reflect
modules.about:
std/reflect: runtime reflection (spec §11.3).

const t = reflect.typeOf(user) // the runtime class of user for (const f of t.fields) println(${f.name}: ${f.type.name} = ${f.show(user)}) const age = t.field("age")!.get(user)

Metadata is generated only for the types that reach reflect.typeOf.

items.name: reflect
items.doc: reflect.typeOf(value) describes the value's runtime class (a subclass of its static type for a class value), reflect.typeOf<T>() the type T; both as a TypeInfo<T>. Metadata is generated only for the types that reach reflect.typeOf.

items.name: TypeInfo
items.doc: A type described at runtime. T is the type it was asked about: for a class value, the description is of the value's runtime class (T or a subclass).

members.name: name
members.doc: As messages show it: Point, Box<i64>, i64[].

members.name: kind
members.doc: "struct", "class", "interface", "enum", "primitive", "array", … (as T.kind).

members.name: fields
members.doc: Instance fields, inherited ones first (private ones only in the declaring module).

members.name: methods
members.doc: Instance methods.

members.name: interfaces
members.doc: The interfaces it declares with implements.

members.name: base
members.doc: The base class.

members.name: decorators
members.doc: The decorators on its declaration, in order.

members.name: constructor
members.signature: constructor( /// As messages show it: `Point`, `Box<i64>`, `i64[]`. public name: string, /// `"struct"`, `"class"`, `"interface"`, `"enum"`, `"primitive"`, `"array"`, … (as `T.kind`). public kind: string, /// Instance fields, inherited ones first (private ones only in the declaring module). public fields: Field<T>[], /// Instance methods. public methods: MethodInfo[], /// The interfaces it declares with `implements`. public interfaces: Type[], /// The base class. public base: TypeInfo<T>?, /// The decorators on its declaration, in order. public decorators: DecoratorInfo[], )
members.doc: Made by the compiler's reflection metadata (reflect.typeOf).

members.name: field
members.doc: The field called name.

members.name: toString
members.doc: Its name.

items.name: Field
items.doc: A field of a T (or of the runtime class described). get and set name the field's type and panic if it's another one (or if the object isn't of the class the field belongs to).

members.name: name
members.doc: The field's name.

members.name: type
members.doc: The field's declared type.

members.name: decorators
members.doc: The decorators on the field, in order.

members.name: isReadonly
members.doc: Whether it's readonly (set panics for it).

members.name: constructor
members.signature: constructor( /// The field's name. public name: string, /// The field's declared type. public type: Type, /// The decorators on the field, in order. public decorators: DecoratorInfo[], /// Whether it's `readonly` (`set` panics for it). public isReadonly: bool, private id: int, )
members.doc: Made by the compiler's reflection metadata.

members.name: get
members.doc: The field's value in obj.

members.name: set
members.signature: public set<V>(obj: T, value: V): void
members.doc: Sets the field in obj (a class instance; a struct is passed by value). Panics for a readonly field (isReadonly).

members.name: show
members.doc: The field's value in obj as a string, as a class's default string form shows it.

members.name: toString
members.doc: As declared: age: int.

items.name: Type
items.doc: A type, as the type of a field or an implemented interface shows it.

members.name: name
members.doc: As messages show it: string, Point, i64[].

members.name: kind
members.doc: "struct", "class", "interface", "enum", "primitive", "array", … (as TypeInfo.kind).

members.name: constructor
members.signature: constructor( /// As messages show it: `string`, `Point`, `i64[]`. public name: string, /// `"struct"`, `"class"`, `"interface"`, `"enum"`, `"primitive"`, `"array"`, … (as /// `TypeInfo.kind`). public kind: string, )
members.doc: Made by the compiler's reflection metadata.

members.name: toString
members.doc: Its name.

examples.code:
import { reflect } from "std/reflect"

struct Size { w: int; h: int }

const f = reflect.typeOf<Size>().field("w")!
println(f.type.toString())   // i64

items.name: DecoratorInfo
items.doc: A decorator on a declaration: its name and each argument's source text (@json.name("id") → json.name, ["\"id\""]).

members.name: name
members.doc: The decorator's name as written: json.name.

members.name: args
members.doc: Each argument's source text: ["\"id\""].

members.name: constructor
members.signature: constructor( /// The decorator's name as written: `json.name`. public name: string, /// Each argument's source text: `["\"id\""]`. public args: string[], )
members.doc: Made by the compiler's reflection metadata.

members.name: toString
members.doc: As written: @json.name("id"), @sealed.

modules.name: std/regex
modules.about: std/regex (spec §13.7): RegExp and its match type. Both are globals (in the core library, <core>/regex.pi); regex literals make RegExps.

items.name: RegExp
items.doc: A regular expression: /pattern/flags or new RegExp(pattern, flags) (flags d, g, i, m, s, u, v, y).

members.name: source
members.doc: The pattern's text ("(?:)" for an empty pattern).

members.name: flags
members.doc: The flags, in canonical order ("dgimsuvy").

members.name: lastIndex
members.doc: Where the next exec or test starts with the g or y flag, in code points; other regexes ignore it.

members.name: constructor
members.signature: constructor(pattern: string, flags: string = "") throws SyntaxError
members.doc: Throws a SyntaxError for an invalid pattern or flags.

members.name: constructor
members.signature: constructor(other: RegExp, flags: string? = null) throws SyntaxError
members.doc: A copy of other: its pattern with its flags, or with flags instead (#62). Its lastIndex starts at 0.

examples.code:
const re = /a+/g
println(new RegExp(re))         // /a+/g
println(new RegExp(re, "i"))    // /a+/i

members.name: global
members.doc: Whether the g flag is set (find every match).

examples.code:
println(/o/g.global)   // true
println(/o/.global)    // false

members.name: ignoreCase
members.doc: Whether the i flag is set (case-insensitive).

examples.code:
const re = /hello/i
println(re.ignoreCase)      // true
println(re.test("HeLLo"))   // true

members.name: multiline
members.doc: Whether the m flag is set (^ and $ also match at line breaks).

examples.code:
const re = /^b/m
println(re.multiline)        // true
println(re.test("a\nb"))     // true

members.name: dotAll
members.doc: Whether the s flag is set (. also matches line breaks).

examples.code:
const re = /a.b/s
println(re.dotAll)          // true
println(re.test("a\nb"))    // true

members.name: unicode
members.doc: Whether the u flag is set.

examples.code:
println(/x/u.unicode)   // true
println(/x/.unicode)    // false

members.name: sticky
members.doc: Whether the y flag is set (a match only at lastIndex).

examples.code:
const re = /\d/y
println(re.sticky)      // true
println(re.test("a1"))  // false
re.lastIndex = 1
println(re.test("a1"))  // true

members.name: hasIndices
members.doc: Whether the d flag is set.

examples.code:
println(/x/d.hasIndices)   // true
println(/x/.hasIndices)    // false

members.name: exec
members.doc: The next match in s (from lastIndex with g or y, which it then moves past the match, or back to 0 when there's none).

members.name: test
members.doc: Whether s has a match (moving lastIndex as exec does).

examples.code:
const digits = /^\d+$/
println(digits.test("123"))   // true
println(digits.test("12a"))   // false

members.name: toString
members.doc: /source/flags.

examples.code:
const re = new RegExp("a/b", "gi")
println(re.toString())   // /a\/b/gi
println(re.source)       // a\/b
println(re.flags)        // gi

const m = /(a)(b)?/d.exec("a")
